summary:
Breuil, Hellmann and Schraen describe the completed local rings of the **trianguline variety** X_tri(r̄) at points of integral weight in terms of the completed local rings of a scheme built from **Grothendieck’s simultaneous resolution**, and draw local and global consequences.

The local model is the scheme X = g̃ ×_g g̃, where g̃ = {(gB,ψ) : Ad(g⁻¹)ψ ∈ b} and q : g̃ → g is the simultaneous resolution. Its irreducible components X_w are indexed by the Weyl group; §2 proves they are reduced, Cohen–Macaulay (Bezrukavnikov–Riche) and — new here — **normal**, and computes cycles on the Steinberg variety through Beilinson–Bernstein and Kazhdan–Lusztig theory. The bridge is Fontaine’s theory of **almost de Rham** B_dR-representations: W ↦ (D_pdR(W), ν_W) is an equivalence onto pairs (vector space, nilpotent operator), Galois-stable B⁺_dR-lattices correspond to filtrations, and a trianguline (φ,Γ_K)-module supplies a second flag. A point of X_tri(r̄) therefore determines a triple (two flags, nilpotent operator), i.e. a point x_pdR of X, and the main local theorem (3.33) says that X̂_tri(r̄)_x and X̂_{w,x_pdR} agree up to formally smooth morphisms. Since the X_w are normal and Cohen–Macaulay, so is X_tri(r̄) at such points (Corollary 3.7.10), hence it is locally irreducible.

The local applications are: flatness of the character and weight maps, the accumulation property, a tangent-space bound that recovers and sharpens the authors’ earlier estimate, the determination of **all** local companion points in the crystalline case (Theorem 4.2.3: exactly the w with w_x ≼ w), and a locally analytic **Breuil–Mézard type** statement (Conjecture 4.3.4, proved for generic crystalline r in Theorem 4.3.8) expressing the cycle of the fibre of X_tri(r̄) over a character as a combination Σ_Π m_{δ,Π}C_{r,Π} with multiplicities from locally analytic principal series.

Globally, for a definite unitary group under the usual Taylor–Wiles hypotheses and via the patched eigenvariety, they prove (i) **classicality**: every generic crystalline strictly dominant point of the Hecke eigenvariety comes from a classical automorphic form; (ii) **companion constituents**: all constituents predicted by Breuil’s conjecture occur in the completed cohomology, so all expected companion points exist; and (iii) **singularities**: the eigenvariety is Cohen–Macaulay with flat weight map at such a point, and is singular there whenever w_xw_0 is not a product of distinct simple reflections. The last is the first systematic source of singular points on eigenvarieties. FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (30 September 2026) corrected the codimension of the character-fibre cycles (E12) and recorded that Lemma 2.3.2 is false as printed (E13). The trianguline variety, Fontaine's almost de Rham theory, completed cohomology, the patched module and the locally analytic inputs now have one owner each. Category O and Kazhdan–Lusztig theory go to the LieHighestWeight Part II.

conventions.K: K/Q_p is finite with Galois group G_K, Γ_K the cyclotomic quotient, ε the cyclotomic character; L/Q_p is finite and splits K, Σ = Hom(K,L), and C_L is the category of local artinian L-algebras with residue field L.
conventions.G: G denotes Spec L ×_{Spec Q_p} Res_{K/Q_p}(GL_{n/K}) ≅ (GL_{n/L})^{[K:Q_p]}, with upper triangular Borel B, torus T, Weyl group S ≅ S_n^{[K:Q_p]}, longest element w_0, length lg and Bruhat order ≼.
conventions.cycles: §4.3 carries two different families of cycles, distinguished in the printed text only by font: 𝖅_{w′}, 𝕮_{w′} of codimension [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 for the fibre over the weight, and 𝒵_{w′}, 𝒞_{w′} of codimension [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 + n for the fibre over the character (printed [K:Q_p]n(n+3)/2; E12). Any formalisation must name them apart.
conventions.conjectures: Conjecture 2.3.7, Conjecture 4.3.4, Conjecture 5.1.1, Conjecture 5.3.1 and Question 4.4.3 are conjectures, not theorems; the items record them as such and they must not be planned as targets.

items.name: Global setting: definite unitary group and its Hecke eigenvariety
items.statement: F⁺ is totally real, F an imaginary quadratic extension of F⁺, G a unitary group in n variables over F⁺ splitting over F and over all p-adic places of F⁺ and compact at all infinite places; S_p the places of F⁺ above p; L/Q_p finite and large enough. Ŝ(U^p,L)^an is the space of overconvergent p-adic automorphic forms of tame level U^p, an admissible locally Q_p-analytic representation of G(F⁺⊗_Q Q_p) ≅ ∏_{v|p} GL_n(F⁺_v). S is a finite set of finite places containing S_p and the v ∤ p where U_v is not hyperspecial, m^S a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra with Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S} ≠ 0, and ρ̄ : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(F̄_p) the associated mod p representation, assumed irreducible. Y(U^p,ρ̄) is the rigid analytic Hecke eigenvariety over L parametrising the finite-slope systems of Hecke eigenvalues in Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S}; a point is a pair (ρ,δ) with ρ a deformation of ρ̄ and δ a locally Q_p-analytic character of the diagonal torus of G(F⁺⊗_Q Q_p).

items.name: Crystalline generic points, the permutations w and w_x, strict dominance
items.statement: A point x = (ρ,δ) is crystalline generic if for every v|p: ρ_v is crystalline; the eigenvalues (φ_{v,i}) of φ^{q_v} on D_cris(ρ_v) satisfy φ_{v,i}φ_{v,j}^{−1} ∉ {1, q_v} for i ≠ j, q_v the residue cardinality of F⁺_v; and the Hodge–Tate weights of ρ_v are regular. To such an x one attaches two elements w = (w_v)_v and w_x = (w_{x,v})_v of S := ∏_{v|p} S_n^{[F⁺_v:Q_p]}: w measures the relative position of the weights of the δ_{v,i} in the antidominant order, w_x the relative position of the two flags coming from the p-adic Hodge theory of ρ_v. x is strictly dominant when w = w_0, equivalently when the algebraic weight of δ is dominant. x′ = (ρ,δ′) is a companion point of x = (ρ,δ) when δ′δ^{−1} is Q_p-algebraic.

items.name: The standing Taylor–Wiles hypotheses (i)–(iv)
items.statement: (i) p > 2; (ii) F/F⁺ is unramified, F contains no non-trivial p-th root of 1, and G is quasi-split at all finite places of F⁺; (iii) U_v is hyperspecial at every finite place v of F⁺ inert in F; (iv) ρ̄(Gal(F̄/F(ᵖ√1))) is adequate in the sense of [66, Def. 2.20].

items.name: Remark 1.1: the missing hypothesis in the authors’ earlier papers
items.statement: The authors record that the assumption ᵖ√1 ∉ F was omitted in a first version of this paper and is also missing in the global results of [19] and [20]: it should be added to [19, Th. 1.5 and Th. 3.5] and all subsequent results, and to [20, Th. 1.1] and the results of [20, §3 and §5]. All results of [19] and [20] remain true with the more general notion of adequate subgroup of [66, Def. 2.20] in place of [65, Def. 2.3].
items.note: This is the authors’ own correction to their two earlier published papers, not to the present one; recorded here because it changes the hypotheses any roadmap must carry for those results.

items.name: Theorem 1.2: classicality of crystalline strictly dominant points
items.statement: Assume (i)–(iv). If x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) is generic crystalline strictly dominant, then x comes from a classical automorphic form of G(A_{F⁺}); in particular ρ is automorphic. Strict dominance is needed for x itself to be classical, but if x is generic crystalline and not strictly dominant there is a generic crystalline strictly dominant x′ = (ρ,δ′) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄), so ρ is automorphic in any case.

items.name: Theorem 1.3: eigenvarieties are singular at sufficiently critical points
items.statement: Assume (i)–(iv) and U^p small enough. If x ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) is generic crystalline strictly dominant and w_xw_0 is not a product of pairwise distinct simple reflections, then x is a singular point of Y(U^p,ρ̄).

items.name: Theorem 1.4: all expected companion constituents occur
items.statement: Assume (i)–(iv) and U^p small enough. If ρ : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(L) comes from a generic crystalline strictly dominant point x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄), then all the companion constituents associated to ρ in [15, §6] and [16, Conj. 6.1] occur, up to twist, as G(F⁺⊗_Q Q_p)-subrepresentations of Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S}[m_ρ]. In particular all companion points x_{w′} of x with w_x ≼ w′ exist in Y(U^p,ρ̄).

items.name: Generic characters of ((F⁺_v)^×)^n
items.statement: A character δ of ((F⁺_v)^×)^n is generic if δ_iδ_j^{−1} and δ_iδ_j^{−1}|·|_v are not Q_p-algebraic characters of (F⁺_v)^× for i ≠ j, |·|_v the norm character.

items.name: The patched eigenvariety and the trianguline variety
items.statement: All the statements hold with Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S} replaced by the patched locally Q_p-analytic representation Π^an_∞ of [23] and Y(U^p,ρ̄) by the patched eigenvariety X_p(ρ̄) of [19, §3.2], which exist only under (i)–(iv). By [19, §3.6], X_p(ρ̄) is a union of irreducible components of 𝔛_{ρ̄^p} × ∏_{v|p} X_tri(ρ̄_v) × U^g, where 𝔛_{ρ̄^p} is the rigid generic fibre of the framed deformation space at the places of S∖S_p, U^g an open polydisc, and X_tri(ρ̄_v) the trianguline variety at v.

items.name: Theorem 1.5: the trianguline variety is normal and Cohen–Macaulay at such points
items.statement: Let x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(ρ̄_v) with δ generic locally algebraic with distinct weights. Then X_tri(ρ̄_v) is normal, hence irreducible, and Cohen–Macaulay in an affinoid neighbourhood of x.

items.name: The point x_pdR and the local model map
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.5, r is almost de Rham in the sense of Fontaine and so is every deformation of r over a nilpotent thickening of L. Fontaine’s equivalence W ↦ (D_pdR(W), ν_W) identifies almost de Rham B_dR-representations with pairs (D,N), N nilpotent, and Galois-stable B⁺_dR-lattices with separated exhaustive ν_W-stable filtrations of D_pdR(W), complete flags when the Sen weights are multiplicity free. With g the Lie algebra of G := (Res_{F⁺_v/Q_p} GL_{n/F⁺_v})_L, b that of the upper Borel, g̃ := {(gB,ψ) ∈ G/B × g : Ad(g^{−1})ψ ∈ b} is smooth irreducible of dimension dim G and g̃ → g is Grothendieck’s simultaneous resolution; X := g̃ ×_g g̃ is equidimensional of dimension dim G with irreducible components X_{w′} indexed by the Weyl group. The two ν-stable flags of D_pdR(r_dR) — the one from the triangulation and the Hodge filtration — give x_pdR := (𝒟_•, Fil_•, N) ∈ X(L), and one obtains a map X̂_tri(ρ̄_v)_x → X̂_{x_pdR} factoring through X̂_{w,x_pdR}.

items.name: Theorem 1.6: the local model theorem
items.statement: For x as in Theorem 1.5, the formal schemes X̂_tri(ρ̄_v)_x and X̂_{w,x_pdR} are isomorphic up to formally smooth morphisms.

items.name: Theorem 1.7: the components X_{w′} are normal and Cohen–Macaulay
items.statement: The algebraic varieties X_{w′} are normal and Cohen–Macaulay for every w′. The Cohen–Macaulay property is due to Bezrukavnikov–Riche; the normality (Theorem 2.3.6) is new to the authors’ knowledge.

items.name: Theorem 1.8: all local companion points in the crystalline case
items.statement: Let x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(ρ̄_v) be as in Theorem 1.5 and crystalline strictly dominant, and let w_x measure the relative position of 𝒟_• and Fil_•. The local companion points of x — the x′ = (r,δ′) ∈ X_tri(ρ̄_v) with δ′δ^{−1} Q_p-algebraic — are parametrised by the w′ with w_x ≼ w′.

items.name: Cycles on the framed deformation ring and the fibres of the trianguline variety
items.statement: R_r is the complete local ring of framed deformations of r over local artinian L-algebras of residue field L, and Z(Spec R_r) the free abelian group on the irreducible closed subschemes; for A a quotient of R_r, [Spec A] := Σ_{𝔭 minimal} m(𝔭,A)[Spec A/𝔭] with m(𝔭,A) the length of A_𝔭 (1.1). For δ generic, (r′,δ′) ↦ r′ gives a closed immersion Spec Ô_{X_tri(ρ̄_v),(r,δ)} ↪ Spec R_r, and X_tri(ρ̄_v)_δ denotes the fibre of the character map above δ, again with a closed immersion into Spec R_r. Although X_tri(ρ̄_v) is reduced, the fibre X_tri(ρ̄_v)_δ can be highly non-reduced and can carry Kazhdan–Lusztig multiplicities.

items.name: Theorem 1.9: a locally analytic Breuil–Mézard type cycle decomposition
items.statement: For any crystalline generic deformation r of ρ̄_v with distinct Hodge–Tate weights and any absolutely irreducible constituent Π of a locally Q_p-analytic principal series of GL_n(F⁺_v), there is a unique cycle 𝒞_{r,Π} of codimension [F⁺_v:Q_p]·n(n+1)/2 + n in Z(Spec R_r) (printed [F⁺_v:Q_p]·n(n+3)/2; E12) such that for all locally Q_p-analytic characters δ, [Spec Ô_{X_tri(ρ̄_v)_δ,(r,δ)}] = Σ_Π m_{δ,Π} 𝒞_{r,Π}, where the left-hand side is 0 if (r,δ) ∉ X_tri(ρ̄_v) and m_{δ,Π} is the multiplicity of Π in the principal series induced from δ suitably normalised.

items.name: The rank-two example: a reducible weight fibre and a ramified weight map
items.statement: For n = 2, F⁺_v = Q_p and r = χ₁ ⊕ χ₂ with χ_i = z^{h_i}unr(φ_i), h₁ < h₂, put δ₁ = z^{h₂}unr(φ₁), δ₂ = z^{h₁}unr(φ₂). Then X_tri(ρ̄_v) is smooth at (r,(δ₁,δ₂)) while Spec Ô_{X_tri(ρ̄_v)_{(δ₁,δ₂)},(r,(δ₁,δ₂))} is reduced with two irreducible components of dimension 3, one from crystalline deformations and one from trianguline non-crystalline ones; the induced principal series has two constituents Π₁ (locally algebraic) and Π₂, and 𝒞_{r,Π₁}, 𝒞_{r,Π₂} are the two component cycles, while for the other ordering 𝒞_{r,Π′₂} = 0. Non-irreducibility of the fibre implies that the projections of X_tri(ρ̄_v) to the character space and to the weight space are not smooth at that point.

items.name: The two cycle identities behind Theorem 1.4
items.statement: For ρ as in Theorem 1.4 and x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) ↪ X_p(ρ̄) generic crystalline strictly dominant, write x_{w′} = (ρ,δ_{w′}) for the companion point attached to w′ ≽ w_x and Π_{w′} for the irreducible socle of the principal series induced from δ_{w′}. With M_∞ the coherent Cohen–Macaulay sheaf of [20, Lem. 3.8] and M̂_{∞,wt(δ),x} its pull-back to the weight fibre, (1.2) [M̂_{∞,wt(δ),x}] = Σ_{w_x ≼ w′} P_{1,w_0w′}(1)[L(w′)] with L(w′) ≠ 0 if and only if Hom(Π_{w′}, Π^an_∞[m_ρ]) ≠ 0, and (1.3) [Ô_{X_p(ρ̄)_{wt(δ)},x}] = Σ_{w_x ≼ w′} P_{1,w_0w′}(1)𝒞(w′) with the 𝒞(w′) non-zero cycles of codimension [F⁺:Q]·n(n+1)/2; 𝒞(w_0) is irreducible and [L(w_0)] ∈ Z_{≥0}𝒞(w_0). (1.2) is representation theory and does not use the local model; (1.3) does.

items.name: Split reductive G in good characteristic, and the Schubert cells
items.statement: G is a split connected reductive group over a field k of good characteristic (char k = 0, or char k > h with h the Coxeter number; only char k = 0 is used later), B ⊃ T a Borel and maximal torus, U the unipotent radical, W = N_G(T)/T with longest element w_0, length lg and Bruhat order ≼; g, b, t, u the Lie algebras and w·λ = w(λ+ρ) − ρ the dot action.
items.note: Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/9). The group-theoretic data (Borel subgroups, the Weyl group, the Bruhat decomposition) are Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 7, and the fppf quotient G/H is Layer 3, where its representability is a theorem with hypotheses. LieGroups Layer 8 is about complex flag manifolds, a different category. Library pointers, cited only as such: tauceti:CoxeterSystem.bruhatPartialOrder (TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Bruhat.lean:240) on an abstract Coxeter system, and tauceti:TauCeti.longestElement (LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/LongestElement.lean:194) and tauceti:TauCeti.dotAction (LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Weyl/DotAction.lean:108) on a root system's Weyl group, not N_G(T)/T. The scheme G/B and the orbits U_w are item 2.1-flag-variety.

items.name: g̃ and the simultaneous resolution
items.statement: g̃ := {(gB,ψ) ∈ G/B × g : Ad(g^{−1})ψ ∈ b} (2.1) is a closed subscheme of dimension dim G, and G ×^B b ≅ g̃ by (g,ψ) ↦ (gB, Ad(g)ψ) (2.2), so g̃ → G/B is a vector bundle and g̃ is smooth and irreducible, a subvector bundle of the trivial bundle G/B × g. The map q : g̃ → g, (gB,ψ) ↦ ψ, is Grothendieck’s simultaneous resolution of singularities. g^reg and g^{reg−ss} denote the regular and regular semisimple loci and g̃^reg, g̃^{reg−ss} their preimages.

items.name: Properties of the simultaneous resolution
items.statement: q is proper and surjective; its restriction to q^{−1}(g^reg) is quasi-finite; and its restriction to q^{−1}(g^{reg−ss}) is étale of degree |W|.

items.name: The scheme X = g̃ ×_g g̃ and the maps π, κ₁, κ₂
items.statement: X := g̃ ×_g g̃ = {(g₁B,g₂B,ψ) ∈ G/B × G/B × g : Ad(g_i^{−1})ψ ∈ b, i = 1,2} (2.3), with π : X → G/B × G/B the projection (2.4) and κ_i : X → t, (g₁B,g₂B,ψ) ↦ image of Ad(g_i^{−1})ψ under b ↠ t (2.5). For w ∈ W, V_w := π^{−1}(U_w).

items.name: V_w → U_w is a vector bundle
items.statement: The projection V_w → U_w induced by π is a geometric vector bundle of relative dimension dim B − lg(w); for y = (gB,gẇB) ∈ U_w the fibre is Ad(g)(t ⊕ (u ∩ Ad(ẇ)u)), an affine space of that dimension (2.6)–(2.7).

items.name: Intersection of two subvector bundles of constant fibre dimension
items.statement: Let V → Y be a geometric vector bundle over a reduced scheme locally of finite type over a field and W₁, W₂ ⊆ V subvector bundles such that for every closed point y the intersection of the fibres is an affine space of constant dimension r. Then the scheme-theoretic intersection W₁ ∩ W₂ is a geometric vector bundle of rank r.

items.name: The closed subsets X_w and the Bruhat constraint
items.statement: X_w is the Zariski closure of V_w in X. For w, w′ ∈ W, X_w ∩ V_{w′} ≠ ∅ implies w′ ≼ w, since π(X_w) is the closure Ū_w of the Schubert cell.

items.name: X is a local complete intersection with components X_w
items.statement: X is locally a complete intersection and its irreducible components are the X_w, w ∈ W; in particular X is Cohen–Macaulay and dim X = dim X_w = dim g = dim G. X ⊆ G/B × G/B × g is equidimensional of dimension dim G and cut out by 2 dim u equations in a smooth scheme.
items.note: Its proof cites "Lemma 2.2.1" for what is Proposition 2.2.1; see source issue E6.

items.name: X is reduced and pr_i restricts to a resolution of g̃
items.statement: X is reduced, hence so is each component X_w with its scheme structure as the scheme-theoretic image of the open stratum. For i = 1,2 the projection pr_i : X → g̃ induces a proper birational morphism pr_{i,w} : X_w → g̃ which is an isomorphism above g̃^reg.

items.name: Equidimensionality of the fibres of κ_i
items.statement: For i = 1,2 the fibres of κ_i and of κ_{i,w} := κ_i|_{X_w} are equidimensional of dimension dim G − dim T, and the restriction of κ_i to each irreducible component of X is surjective. The proof uses the G_m-action λ·(g₁B,g₂B,ψ) = (g₁B,g₂B,λψ) and the description of π^{−1}(U_w) ∩ κ₁^{−1}(0) as a vector bundle over U_w with fibre u ∩ Ad(w)u.

items.name: Miracle flatness
items.statement: Let f : Y → Z be a morphism of noetherian schemes with Z regular and Y Cohen–Macaulay, such that dim O_{Y,y} = dim O_{Z,f(y)} + dim O_{f⁻¹(f(y)),y} for every y ∈ Y. Then f is flat. The local equality holds when Y is equidimensional and f is a morphism of schemes of finite type over a field with Z irreducible; the paper's printed global hypothesis (all fibres equidimensional of dimension dim Y − dim Z) does not imply it in general (E13).
items.note: Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/10); cf. Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, Theorem 23.1, and EGA IV 6.1.5. Every use in the paper satisfies the corrected hypothesis: κ_{i,w} on the irreducible X_w (p. 316) and f₁ on V_w (p. 317), with X equidimensional; on p. 408 the lemma is applied to spectra of local rings, where the hypothesis at the closed fibre is the local equality.

items.name: X_w is Cohen–Macaulay and the weight maps are flat
items.statement: The schemes X_w are Cohen–Macaulay and the morphisms κ_i and κ_{i,w} are flat for i = 1,2. In characteristic > h this is Bezrukavnikov–Riche; the characteristic-zero case is obtained by spreading out over Z_{(p)} with a Chevalley model.

items.name: κ₂ = Ad(w^{−1})∘κ₁ on X_w
items.statement: For w ∈ W one has κ_{2,w} = Ad(w^{−1}) ∘ κ_{1,w}, so that the square formed by κ_{1,w}, κ_{2,w} and the two projections t → t/W commutes (2.9).

items.name: (π,κ_i) is smooth on V_w with irreducible fibres
items.statement: For w ∈ W the fixed subscheme t^w ⊂ t of Ad(w) is smooth and irreducible. The restriction of (π,κ_i) : X → G/B × G/B × t to V_w is a smooth map V_w → U_w × t with irreducible fibres; in particular V_w ∩ κ_i^{−1}(t^{w′}) is irreducible for all w, w′.

items.name: The components X_w are normal
items.statement: The schemes X_w are normal. Since they are Cohen–Macaulay it suffices to prove regularity in codimension one; a codimension-one component C of X_w ∖ V_w would lie in V_{w′} ∩ κ₁^{−1}(t^{ww′^{−1}}) for some w′, and codimension counting forces ww′^{−1} to be a reflection s_α with lg(w′) < lg(s_αw′), whence C meets pr_{1,w}^{−1}(g̃^reg), where X_w is smooth.
items.note: The paper states this normality is new; it is what makes the trianguline variety normal at the points of Corollary 3.7.10.

items.name: Conjecture 2.3.7 on the strata of X_w
items.statement: CONJECTURE (not proved in this paper). For w, w′ ∈ W with w′ ≼ w and w̃ = ww′^{−1}, X_w ∩ V_{w′} = V_{w′} ∩ κ₁^{−1}(t^{w̃}). Lemma 2.3.4 gives the inclusion ⊆.
items.note: A conjecture, not a theorem: it must not be planned as a target. Remark 2.5.4 and Remark 4.1.6(iii) record what it would give.

items.name: The Steinberg variety and the Springer resolution
items.statement: Assume char k = 0. With g/G := Spec(R_g^G) and t/W ≅ g/G, let κ̄ : X → g/G be the composite of X → g with g ↠ g/G. Z := (κ̄^{−1}(0))^red (2.11) is the Steinberg variety, and Z ≅ Ñ ×_𝒩 Ñ where 𝒩 is the nilpotent cone, Ñ := {(gB,ψ) ∈ G/B × 𝒩 : Ad(g^{−1})ψ ∈ u} ≅ G ×^B u (2.12) and Ñ → 𝒩 is the Springer resolution. V′_w := π^{−1}(U_w) ∩ Z and Z_w is its closure with the reduced structure.

items.name: Components of the Steinberg variety
items.statement: Z is equidimensional of dimension dim G − dim T and its irreducible components are the Z_w, w ∈ W.

items.name: What is not known about the Z_w
items.statement: Contrary to the X_w, it does not seem to be known whether the components Z_w of the Steinberg variety are Cohen–Macaulay, and even granting that, the proof of Theorem 2.3.6 does not extend; the authors do not know whether the Z_w are normal.

items.name: Top-dimensional cycles on Z and the class of a scheme
items.statement: Z⁰(Z) is the free abelian group on the irreducible components of Z, so the [Z_w] form a basis and Z⁰(Z) ≅ Z[W]. For Y whose space is a union of components of Z, [Y] := Σ_w m(Z_w,Y)[Z_w] (2.13) with m(Z_w,Y) the length of O_{Y,η_w} at the generic point of Z_w. X̄_w := κ_{1,w}^{−1}(0) (not reduced) has every component of dimension exactly dim Z, hence of the form Z_{w′}.

items.name: Verma modules M(μ) and their irreducible quotients L(μ)
items.statement: M(μ) = U(g) ⊗_{U(b)} k(μ) is the Verma module of highest weight μ, and L(μ) its unique irreducible quotient.
items.note: Split by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/1). Tau Ceti LieHighestWeight Layer 3 plans PBW, Verma modules and L(λ); Tau Ceti has tauceti:TauCeti.VermaModule (TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/HighestWeight/Verma.lean:196) and tauceti:TauCeti.irreducibleQuotient (:416). Their limits: the file assumes a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with non-degenerate Killing form, and says that 'What is not proved here is that M(lam) is nonzero'; so the item stays planned, not library. Category O, the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials and the multiplicity theorem are items 2.4-category-O-block, 2.4-kl-polynomials and 2.4-kl-theorem (route 8); Layers 6 and 7 of LieHighestWeight exclude category O.

items.name: The Beilinson–Bernstein equivalence and the D-modules 𝔐, 𝔏
items.statement: O(0) is the block of trivial infinitesimal character. The Beilinson–Bernstein correspondence gives an exact equivalence BB_G : O(0) ≅ D−Mod^{rh}_{G/B×G/B} onto regular holonomic G-equivariant D-modules on G/B × G/B, obtained from the usual B-equivariant equivalence on G/B by extending along gB ↦ (B,gB). One writes 𝔐(ww_0·0) and 𝔏(ww_0·0) for the images of M(ww_0·0) and L(ww_0·0).

items.name: Characteristic varieties lie in the Steinberg variety
items.statement: Z is the union inside T^*(G/B × G/B) of the conormal bundles of the diagonal G-orbits U_w, and Z_w is the closure of T^*_{U_w}(G/B × G/B). For 𝔐 regular holonomic G-equivariant, Ch(𝔐)^red ⊆ Z, so the characteristic cycle [𝔐] := [Ch(𝔐)] ∈ Z⁰(Z) is defined and additive.
items.locator: Proposition 2.4.4 with the surrounding text, printed pp. 321–322

items.name: The Kazhdan–Lusztig irreducibility conjecture is false in general
items.statement: Kazhdan and Lusztig conjectured for G = SL_n that [𝔏(ww_0·0)] = Z_w, i.e. that the characteristic cycles are irreducible; this is false for n ≥ 8 and true for n ≤ 7.

items.name: The fibre X̄_w is the characteristic cycle of the Verma D-module
items.statement: For w ∈ W, [X̄_w] = [𝔐(ww_0·0)] in Z⁰(Z).

items.name: Three bases of Z⁰(Z) and the multiplicity matrices
items.statement: (i) The families ([Z_w]), ([𝔐(ww_0·0)]) and ([𝔏(ww_0·0)]) are bases of Z⁰(Z). (ii) [𝔐(ww_0·0)] = Σ_{w′} P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1)[𝔏(w′w_0·0)]. (iii) There are integers a_{w,w′} ∈ Z_{≥0} with [𝔏(ww_0·0)] = Σ_{w′} a_{w,w′}[Z_{w′}], a_{w,w} = 1, a_{w,w′} = 0 unless w′ ≼ w, and a_{w,w′} = 0 whenever w′ ≺ w and U_{w′} lies in the smooth locus of Ū_w. Consequently X̄_w contains every Z_{w′} with w′ ≼ w, in general with multiplicities.
items.note: Its proof prints "P_{w,w′}(1) = 0 unless w′ ≼ w", dropping the w₀ prefixes; see source issue E7. Part (ii) uses the Kazhdan–Lusztig multiplicity theorem, item 2.4-kl-theorem, imported from route 8 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/1).

items.name: The characteristic cycle is invariant under the parabolic P_w
items.statement: Let P_w ⊆ G be the largest parabolic containing B whose Levi M_w makes ww_0·0 dominant for M_w ∩ B; the B-action on L(ww_0·0) extends to P_w. Then [𝔏(ww_0·0)] ∈ Z⁰(Z) is invariant under every element of P_w(k), and consequently h(Z_{w′}) = Z_{w′} for every h ∈ P_w(k) whenever a_{w,w′} ≠ 0.

items.name: The scheme T = t ×_{t/W} t and its components
items.statement: By Lemma 2.3.4 the map (κ₁,κ₂) : X → t × t factors through T := t ×_{t/W} t. The irreducible components of T are the T_w = {(z, Ad(w^{−1})z) : z ∈ t}, and X_w is the unique component of X with (κ₁,κ₂)(X_w) = T_w.

items.name: The completion detects the component
items.statement: Let x be a closed point of X and w ∈ W with x ∈ X_w. For w′ ∈ W, the composite X̂_{w,x} ↪ X̂_x → T̂_{(κ₁,κ₂)(x)} factors through T̂_{w′,(κ₁,κ₂)(x)} if and only if w′ = w. The proof uses that for an excellent local reduced ring whose quotients by the minimal primes are normal, completion induces a bijection on minimal primes — which is where the normality of Theorem 2.3.6 enters.
items.note: Its proof prints the ambient scheme of η̂_{T_w} as Spec Ô_{X,x} instead of Spec Ô_{T,(κ₁,κ₂)(x)}; see source issue E7.

items.name: Tangent-space bound and a smoothness criterion for X_w
items.statement: Let x ∈ X_w be a closed point whose image in g is 0 and w′ ∈ W with x ∈ X_w ∩ V_{w′}. (i) dim T_{X_w,x} ≤ dim T_{Ū_w,π(x)} + dim t^{ww′^{−1}} + lg(w′w_0). (ii) If t^{ww′^{−1}} has codimension lg(w) − lg(w′) in t and Ū_w is smooth at π(x), then X_w is smooth at x. Granting Conjecture 2.3.7 for w = w_0, the inequality in (i) is an equality for w = w_0.

items.name: Cycles commute with completion, and the completed KL decomposition
items.statement: For a coherent module ℳ on X̄ := κ₁^{−1}(0) and a closed point x of X̄, [ℳ̂_x] = Σ_w m(Z_w,ℳ)[Spec Ô_{Z_w,x}] in Z⁰(Spec Ô_{Z,x}) (Lemma 2.5.5). Setting [𝔏̂(ww_0·0)_x] := Σ_{w′} a_{w,w′}[Spec Ô_{Z_{w′},x}] (2.16), one obtains [Ô_{X̄_w,x}] = Σ_{w′} P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1)[𝔏̂(w′w_0·0)_x] (Corollary 2.5.6).

items.name: B_dR-representations and almost de Rham representations
items.statement: A B_dR-representation of G_K is a finite dimensional B_dR-vector space with a continuous semilinear G_K-action; every one contains a G_K-stable B⁺_dR-lattice. W is almost de Rham if it contains a G_K-stable B⁺_dR-lattice W⁺ whose associated C-representation W⁺/tW⁺ has all Sen weights in Z; de Rham implies almost de Rham. The almost de Rham representations form a tannakian subcategory Rep_pdR(G_K) stable under kernels, cokernels and extensions.
items.note: Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/3): missing. PadicHodgeTheory P7's packet has nothing on almost de Rham representations, B_pdR, D_pdR, G_a, B-pairs or W_dR. Routed to the PadicHodgeTheory Part II of PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18 route 5 (route 4). The Sen weights in its definition come from PadicHodgeTheory:P7/sen-module.

items.name: The rings B⁺_pdR, B_pdR, the derivation ν and the functor D_pdR
items.statement: B⁺_pdR := B⁺_dR[log t] and B_pdR := B_dR ⊗_{B⁺_dR} B⁺_pdR, with G_K acting by g(log t) = log t + log ε(g); ν_{B_pdR} is the unique B_dR-derivation with ν(log t) = −1, preserving B⁺_pdR and commuting with G_K. D_pdR(W) := (B_pdR ⊗_{B_dR} W)^{G_K} is a K-vector space with dim_K D_pdR(W) ≤ dim_{B_dR} W, and W is almost de Rham precisely when equality holds.
items.note: Routed by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/3) with Fontaine's theory to the PadicHodgeTheory Part II (route 4).

items.name: Fontaine’s equivalence: almost de Rham representations are pairs (V, ν)
items.statement: For a field E of characteristic 0, Rep_E(G_a) is equivalent to the category of pairs (V, ν_V) with ν_V nilpotent. D_pdR, with the G_a-action induced by ν_{B_pdR} ⊗ 1, induces an equivalence Rep_pdR(G_K) ≅ Rep_K(G_a); a quasi-inverse is (V,ν_V) ↦ (B_pdR ⊗_K V)^{ν⊗1+1⊗ν_V=0}, both functors are exact, and there is a comparison isomorphism ρ_pdR : B_pdR ⊗_K D_pdR(W) ≅ B_pdR ⊗_{B_dR} W (3.2).
items.note: Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/3): missing. PadicHodgeTheory P7's packet has nothing on almost de Rham representations, B_pdR, D_pdR, G_a, B-pairs or W_dR. Routed to the PadicHodgeTheory Part II of PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18 route 5 (route 4).

items.name: The coefficient version of the equivalence
items.statement: For A a finite dimensional Q_p-algebra, an A⊗_{Q_p}B_dR-representation is a B_dR-representation with an A-action making it finite free over A⊗_{Q_p}B_dR. D_pdR induces an equivalence between the almost de Rham ones, Rep_{pdR,A}(G_K), and Rep_{A⊗_{Q_p}K}(G_a); in particular W is free over A⊗B_dR iff D_pdR(W) is free over A⊗K. Every A⊗B_dR-representation contains a B⁺_dR-lattice preserved by A.
items.note: Routed by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/3) with Fontaine's theory to the PadicHodgeTheory Part II (route 4).

items.name: The deformation groupoids X_W and X^□_W
items.statement: With G := Spec L ×_{Spec Q_p} Res_{K/Q_p}(GL_{n/K}) and g̃, X as in §2.1 over k = L: for W an almost de Rham L⊗B_dR-representation of rank n, X_W is the groupoid over C_L of triples (A,W_A,ι_A) deforming W, and X^□_W adds a framing α_A : (A⊗_{Q_p}K)^n ≅ D_pdR(W_A) lifting a fixed α. Any deformation of W is automatically almost de Rham. X^□_W → X_W is formally smooth and X^□_W → |X^□_W| is an equivalence, because a framed automorphism is the identity on D_pdR.

items.name: X^□_W is the completion of g at N_W
items.statement: The groupoid X^□_W is pro-representable and (W_A,ι_A,α_A) ↦ N_{W_A} — the matrix of α_A^{−1}∘ν_{W_A}∘α_A — identifies |X^□_W| with ĝ, the completion of g at N_W. In particular |X^□_W| is pro-represented by a power series ring in n²[K:Q_p] variables. The unframed |X_W| is not pro-representable, though it has a hull.

items.name: The filtered framed groupoid is the completion of g̃
items.statement: A filtered A⊗B_dR-representation (W,F_•) is one with an increasing filtration by subrepresentations whose graded pieces are free of rank one (Definition 3.1.8). For (W,F_•) with W almost de Rham, X_{W,F_•} and X^□_{W,F_•} := X_{W,F_•} ×_{X_W} X^□_W are defined; the functor (W_A,F_{A,•},ι_A,α_A) ↦ (α_A^{−1}(𝒟_{A,•}), N_{W_A}), with 𝒟_{A,i} = D_pdR(F_{A,i}), identifies |X^□_{W,F_•}| with the completion ĝ̃ of g̃ at (α^{−1}(𝒟_•), N_W), a formally smooth complete local ring of dimension n²[K:Q_p].

items.name: The weight morphism κ_{W,F_•}
items.statement: With κ : g̃ → t the weight map of §2.3, which sends (α^{−1}(𝒟_•),N_W) to 0 since N_W is nilpotent, κ_{W,F_•} is the composite X^□_{W,F_•} ≅ ĝ̃ → t̂; it factors through X_{W,F_•} → t̂ independently of the framing, and on points κ_{W,F_•}(x_A) = (ν_{A,1},…,ν_{A,n}) where ν_{A,i} is the endomorphism induced by ν_{W_A} on 𝒟_{A,i}/𝒟_{A,i−1} (3.4).

items.name: Lattices correspond to filtrations
items.statement: For W in Rep_pdR(G_K) and a G_K-stable B⁺_dR-lattice W⁺ ⊆ W, set Fil^i_{W⁺}(D_pdR(W)) := (t^iB⁺_pdR ⊗_{B⁺_dR} W⁺)^{G_K} (3.5); the i with non-zero graded piece are the opposites of the Sen weights of W⁺/tW⁺. The map W⁺ ↦ Fil^•_{W⁺}(D_pdR(W)) is a bijection between the G_K-stable B⁺_dR-lattices of W and the filtrations of D_pdR(W) as a G_a-representation.
items.note: Formula (3.6) in the proof prints D_dR(W) for D_pdR(W); see source issue E8.

items.name: The B⁺_dR-analogue of the coefficient equivalence
items.statement: W⁺ ↦ (D_pdR(W⁺[1/t]), Fil^•_{W⁺}) is an equivalence between almost de Rham A⊗_{Q_p}B⁺_dR-representations of G_K and filtered A⊗_{Q_p}K-representations of G_a — pairs (V, Fil^•) with Fil^• decreasing, exhaustive and separated by subobjects whose graded pieces are finite projective A⊗_{Q_p}K-modules (for A in C_L: τ-components free A-modules of finite type). Moreover for any finite type A-module M there is a natural isomorphism M ⊗_A gr^i_{Fil^•_{W⁺}}(D_pdR(W⁺[1/t])) ≅ gr^i_{Fil^•_{M⊗_AW⁺}}(D_pdR(M⊗_AW⁺[1/t])).
items.note: The printed definition of a filtered representation requires the graded pieces to be free of rank one "for i ∈ Z", which is impossible for an exhaustive separated filtration; see source issue E8. The corrected condition on the graded pieces is 'finite projective', not 'free', over A⊗_{Q_p}K (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/11).

items.name: The graded pieces are constant in a deformation
items.statement: For A in C_L, W⁺_A an almost de Rham A⊗B⁺_dR-representation deforming W⁺, and every τ ∈ Σ and i ∈ Z, gr^i_{Fil^•_{W⁺_A}}(D_{pdR,τ}(W_A)) ⊗_A L ≅ gr^i_{Fil^•_{W⁺}}(D_{pdR,τ}(W)); in particular the non-zero graded pieces occur exactly at the i = −h_{τ,j}.

items.name: Regular lattices and the second description of ĝ̃
items.statement: W⁺ is regular if for each τ the integers h_{τ,i} are pairwise distinct. For W⁺ regular, Fil_{W⁺_A,i}(D_pdR(W_A)) := ⊕_{τ∈Σ} Fil^{−h_{τ,i}}_{W⁺_A}(D_{pdR,τ}(W_A)) (3.9) is a complete flag stable under ν_{W_A}, and (W⁺_A,ι_A,α_A) ↦ (α_A^{−1}(Fil_{W⁺_A,•}), N_{W_A}) identifies |X^□_{W⁺}| with the completion of g̃ at (α^{−1}(Fil_{W⁺,•}), N_W) — a different point of g̃(L) from the one in §3.1, the two being mixed in §3.5. The associated weight map is κ_{W⁺} : X_{W⁺} → t̂.
items.note: The completion point is printed without α^{−1}, and the weight map is said to use "the isomorphism of Corollary 3.2.5" where 3.2.5 is a Theorem; see source issue E8.

items.name: (φ,Γ_K)-modules over the Robba ring and after inverting t
items.statement: A (φ,Γ_K)-module over R_K[1/t] is a finite free R_K[1/t]-module with commuting semilinear φ and Γ_K-action admitting a (φ,Γ_K)-stable R_K-lattice; with A-coefficients one requires finite freeness over R_{A,K}[1/t]. The categories are written ΦΓ⁺_K, ΦΓ_K and ΦΓ_{A,K}. A module is of character type if it is isomorphic to R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t] for a continuous δ : K^× → A^×.

items.name: Algebraic, constant, smooth and locally algebraic characters
items.statement: A continuous δ : K^× → A^× is algebraic if δ(z) = ∏_{τ∈Σ} τ(z)^{k_τ}, written z^k; constant if it factors through L^×; smooth if wt(δ) = 0; and locally algebraic if it is a product of a smooth and an algebraic character, equivalently if wt_τ(δ) ∈ Z for all τ. With Lubin–Tate elements t_τ, every non-zero (φ,Γ_K)-submodule of R_{L,K}(δ)[1/t] over R_{L,K} is t^kR_{L,K}(δ) for some k ∈ Z^{[K:Q_p]}.

items.name: (φ,γ_K)-cohomology and its comparison with Ext groups
items.statement: H^i_{φ,γ_K}(M) is the cohomology of the Herr-type complex (3.10). For D ⊆ M with M = D[1/t], H^i_{φ,γ_K}(M) = colim_n H^i_{φ,γ_K}(t^{−n}D) (3.11), and H^1_{φ,γ_K}(M) ≅ Ext^1_{ΦΓ_K}(R_K[1/t],M) (3.12); the pull-back Ext^1_{ΦΓ_{A,K}}(R_{A,K}[1/t],M) → Ext^1_{ΦΓ_K}(R_K[1/t],M) is an isomorphism (3.13). H^0_{φ,γ_K} is left exact with H^0_{φ,γ_K}(R_{A,K}[1/t]) = A, and dim H^0_{φ,γ_K}(R_{A,K}(δ)) ≤ dim H^0_{φ,γ_K}(R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t]) ≤ dim A (3.14).

items.name: Cohomology of R_{L,K}(δ)/t^kR_{L,K}(δ)
items.statement: For k ∈ Z^{[K:Q_p]}_{≥0}, δ : K^× → L^× continuous and j ∈ {0,1}: if wt_τ(δ) ∉ {1−k_τ,…,0} for every τ then H^j_{φ,γ_K}(R_{L,K}(δ)/t^kR_{L,K}(δ)) = 0; if wt_τ(δ) ∈ {1−k_τ,…,0} for every τ then it has dimension [K:Q_p] over L.

items.name: Rigidity of the parameter after inverting t
items.statement: If R_{A,K}(δ₁)[1/t] ≅ R_{A,K}(δ₂)[1/t] then δ₂δ₁^{−1} is a constant algebraic character K^× → L^×.

items.name: The functors W⁺_dR and W_dR and their freeness
items.statement: W⁺_dR is Berger’s functor from (φ,Γ_K)-modules over R_K to B⁺_dR-representations, and W_dR(M) := B_dR ⊗_{B⁺_dR} W⁺_dR(D) for any D with M = D[1/t], independent of D. If D is of rank n over R_{A,K} then W⁺_dR(D) is finite free of rank n over A⊗_{Q_p}B⁺_dR, and if M is of rank n over R_{A,K}[1/t] then W_dR(M) is finite free of rank n over A⊗_{Q_p}B_dR. Both functors are exact.
