PadicHodgeTheory P7's packet has nothing on almost de Rham representations, B_pdR, D_pdR, G_a, B-pairs or W_dR. Routed to the PadicHodgeTheory Part II of PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18 route 5 (route 4).

items.name: When W_dR of a rank-one module is almost de Rham
items.statement: Let δ : K^× → A^× be continuous and M := R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t]. If δ̄ := δ mod m_A is smooth then W_dR(M) is almost de Rham with wt(δ) = ν_{W_dR(M)}; more generally if δ̄ is locally algebraic then W_dR(M) is almost de Rham with wt(δ) = wt(δ̄) + ν_{W_dR(M)}. Moreover W_dR(R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t]) is trivial if and only if δ is locally algebraic.

items.name: Trianguline modules, triangulations and parameters
items.statement: M in ΦΓ_{A,K} of rank n is trianguline if it has an increasing filtration M_• by subobjects with M_1 and the M_i/M_{i−1} of character type; M_• is a triangulation and the δ_i with M_i/M_{i−1} ≅ R_{A,K}(δ_i)[1/t] form a parameter. A triangulation is a filtration by direct factors, and by Lemma 3.3.4 either all parameters of M_• are locally algebraic or none is.

items.name: The deformation groupoids of a trianguline module and the character space
items.statement: X_{M,M_•} is the groupoid over C_L of deformations (M_A, M_{A,•}, j_A) of M with its triangulation, and X_M the version without the triangulation. T is the rigid space of continuous characters of K^×; the functor of deformations of a parameter δ is pro-represented by the completion T̂^n_δ of T^n_L at δ, and (M_A,M_{A,•},j_A) ↦ δ_A gives ω_δ : X_{M,M_•} → T̂^n_δ, with ω_{δ′} = (×δ′δ^{−1})∘ω_δ for another parameter (3.15). The framed versions are X^□_M := X_M ×_{X_W} X^□_W and X^□_{M,M_•} := X_{M,M_•} ×_{X_{W,F_•}} X^□_{W,F_•}.

items.name: Parameters and the ν-weight map agree
items.statement: Setting F_i := W_dR(M_i), if M_• has a locally algebraic parameter then W := W_dR(M) is almost de Rham with the filtration F_•, and the square formed by X_{M,M_•} → X_{W,F_•}, ω_δ, κ_{W,F_•} and wt − wt(δ) : T̂^n_δ → t̂ (3.16) commutes. Hence a morphism X_{M,M_•} → T̂^n_δ ×_{t̂} X_{W,F_•} (3.17).
items.note: Formula (3.16) is printed with the tuple index inside the difference; see source issue E8.

items.name: The comparison map from (φ,γ_K)-cohomology to Galois cohomology
items.statement: For W an almost de Rham A⊗B_dR-representation, Ext^1 in Rep_{pdR,A}(G_K) agrees with Ext^1 in all A⊗B_dR-representations and with H^1(G_K,W) (3.18); exactness of W_dR then gives a functorial A⊗K-linear map H^1_{φ,γ_K}(M) → H^1(G_K,W_dR(M)) (3.19). Through Fontaine’s equivalence, H^0(G_K,W) ≅ ker(ν_W) and H^1(G_K,W) ≅ coker(ν_W), so H^1(G_K,−) is right exact on Rep_pdR(G_K) and exact on de Rham representations.

items.name: Comparison of H¹ before and after inverting t
items.statement: Let δ : K^× → L^× be continuous with δ and εδ^{−1} not algebraic, and k ∈ Z^{[K:Q_p]}_{≥0}. Then H^0_{φ,γ_K}(t^{−k}R_{L,K}(δ)) = H^2_{φ,γ_K}(R_{L,K}(δ)) = 0; the map H^1_{φ,γ_K}(R_{L,K}(δ)) → H^1_{φ,γ_K}(t^{−k}R_{L,K}(δ)) is an isomorphism if wt_τ(δ) ∉ {1,…,k_τ} for all τ, and is zero if wt_τ(δ) ∈ {1,…,k_τ} for all τ. Both spaces have dimension [K:Q_p].

items.name: The comparison is an isomorphism in rank one
items.statement: For δ : K^× → L^× locally algebraic with δ and εδ^{−1} not algebraic, the map of (3.19) H^1_{φ,γ_K}(R_{L,K}(δ)[1/t]) → H^1(G_K, W_dR(R_{L,K}(δ)[1/t])) ≅ H^1(G_K, L⊗_{Q_p}B_dR) is an isomorphism.

items.name: The comparison over artinian coefficients
items.statement: Let A be in C_L and δ : K^× → A^× continuous with δ̄ and εδ̄^{−1} not algebraic. Then H^0_{φ,γ_K}(R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t]) = H^2_{φ,γ_K}(R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t]) = 0; if δ̄ is locally algebraic the comparison map to H^1(G_K, W_dR(R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t])) is surjective; and if δ itself is locally algebraic it is an isomorphism.

items.name: The genericity locus T_0 and T^n_0
items.statement: T_0 ⊂ T_L is the complement of the L-points z^k and ε(z)z^k, k ∈ Z^{[K:Q_p]}; T^n_0 consists of the δ = (δ_1,…,δ_n) with δ_i/δ_j ∈ T_0 for i ≠ j, i.e. the complement of those for which δ_iδ_j^{−1} OR εδ_iδ_j^{−1} is algebraic for SOME i ≠ j. If a triangulation admits a parameter in T^n_0(L) then all its parameters lie there.
items.note: The printed equivalent description says "δ_iδ_j^{−1} and εδ_iδ_j^{−1} are algebraic for i ≠ j", which can never hold, so as printed T^n_0 = T^n_L; see source issue E2. The statement above is the corrected one.

items.name: The key formal smoothness theorem
items.statement: Let M be trianguline of rank n over R_{L,K}[1/t] with triangulation M_• and parameter δ, and assume δ is locally algebraic and lies in T^n_0(L). With W := W_dR(M) and F_• := W_dR(M_•), the morphism X_{M,M_•} → T̂^n_δ ×_{t̂} X_{W,F_•} of (3.17) is formally smooth. The proof builds the deformation step by step, reducing to the surjectivity of a fibre-product map (3.23) via Lemma 3.4.3 and a base-change identity for H^1(G_K,−) coming from coker(ν).

items.name: A surjectivity lemma for fibre products of modules
items.statement: For a ring A, an ideal I with B := A/I and a surjection f : M ↠ N of A-modules, the map M → (M⊗_AB) ×_{N⊗_AB} N, m ↦ (m⊗1, f(m)), is surjective.

items.name: Forgetting the triangulation is a closed immersion
items.statement: A morphism of groupoids over C_L is a closed immersion if it is relatively representable and each representing map of complete local rings is a surjection. For M trianguline with triangulation M_• and parameter δ ∈ T^n_0(L), the morphism X_{M,M_•} → X_M is relatively representable and a closed immersion, because the deforming triangulation is unique.
items.locator: Proposition 3.4.6 with the preceding definition, printed p. 354

items.name: Vanishing ν forces the deformation to split
items.statement: Let M be trianguline with triangulation M_• and locally algebraic parameter δ ∈ T^n_0(L), and let (A,M_A,M_{A,•},j_A) be an object of X_{M,M_•} such that the nilpotent endomorphism ν_{W_dR(M_A)} vanishes. Then M_{A,i} = ⊕_{j≤i} R_{A,K}(δ_{A,j})[1/t] for every i, so M_A, and hence M, is split.

items.name: Deformations of a (φ,Γ_K)-module split into a t-inverted and a lattice part
items.statement: For D a (φ,Γ_K)-module over R_{L,K} with W⁺_dR(D) almost de Rham, the groupoid X_D of deformations of D is equivalent to X_{D[1/t]} ×_{X_{W_dR(D[1/t])}} X_{W⁺_dR(D)}. The proof rests on Berger’s equivalence between (φ,Γ_K)-modules over R_K and B-pairs, and on the rank-preserving equivalence between ΦΓ_{A,K} and A⊗_{Q_p}B_e-representations of G_K, B_e = B_cris^{φ=1}, given by M ↦ W_e(M) with quasi-inverse W_e ↦ D(W_e,W⁺_dR)[1/t].
items.locator: Proposition 3.5.1 and its proof, printed p. 355
items.note: Its B-pair input is item 3.5-bpairs-berger (route 4; RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/3).

items.name: Freeness criterion and existence of free lattices
items.statement: A (φ,Γ_K)-module D with an A-action is free over R_{A,K} if and only if D[1/t] is free over R_{A,K}[1/t] and W⁺_dR(D) is free over A⊗_{Q_p}B⁺_dR. Consequently any M in ΦΓ_{A,K} with W_dR(M) almost de Rham possesses a free R_{A,K}-lattice stable under φ and Γ_K.

items.name: The trianguline groupoids X_{D,M_•} and their framed and filtered companions
items.statement: For D trianguline of rank n with M := D[1/t] and a triangulation M_• possessing a locally algebraic parameter, put W⁺ := W⁺_dR(D), W := W_dR(M) and F_• := W_dR(M_•). Then X_{D,M_•} := X_D ×_{X_M} X_{M,M_•}, X^□_D := X_D ×_{X_W} X^□_W, X_{W⁺,F_•} := X_{W⁺} ×_{X_W} X_{W,F_•} and their framed versions are defined; in each of them one deforms the filtration on M = D[1/t], resp. on W = W⁺[1/t], and not a triangulation on D itself.

items.name: Relative representability of the comparison morphisms
items.statement: Under the running hypotheses (D trianguline, M_• with a parameter in T^n_0(L)), the morphisms X_M → X_W and X_{M,M_•} → X_{W,F_•} are relatively representable, and so are X^□_{M,M_•} → X^□_{W,F_•}, X_{D,M_•} → X_{W⁺,F_•} and X^□_{D,M_•} → X^□_{W⁺,F_•}.

items.name: Formal smoothness of the comparison morphisms
items.statement: The morphism wt − wt(δ) : T̂^n_δ → t̂ is formally smooth of relative dimension n (Lemma 3.5.5), and hence the morphisms X_{M,M_•} → X_{W,F_•}, X^□_{M,M_•} → X^□_{W,F_•}, X_{D,M_•} → X_{W⁺,F_•} and X^□_{D,M_•} → X^□_{W⁺,F_•} are formally smooth.

items.name: Pro-representability and dimension of the framed trianguline groupoid
items.statement: X^□_{M,M_•} is pro-representable and |X^□_{M,M_•}| is pro-represented by a formally smooth complete local ring of residue field L and dimension [K:Q_p](n² + n(n+1)/2). The proof uses the rigidified groupoid X^ver_{M,M_•}, in which the isomorphisms of the graded pieces are also deformed; it is pro-represented by a formally smooth ring of dimension n + [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2.
items.locator: Proposition 3.5.7 and its proof, printed pp. 358–359

items.name: The framed filtered lattice groupoid is the completion of X at x_pdR
items.statement: With W⁺ regular, put x := (α^{−1}(𝒟_•), α^{−1}(Fil_{W⁺,•}), N_W) ∈ X(L), the triple of the two flags and the nilpotent operator. Then X^□_{W⁺,F_•} is pro-representable with |X^□_{W⁺,F_•}| ≅ X̂_x, and X^□_{D,M_•} is pro-representable and formally smooth of relative dimension [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 over X̂_x.

items.name: The w-components and the set S(x)
items.statement: For w in the Weyl group S, X^{□,w}_{W⁺,F_•} := X^□_{W⁺,F_•} ×_{|X^□_{W⁺,F_•}|} X̂_{w,x} (3.25), and X^w_{W⁺,F_•} is its image under forgetting the framing, independent of α by G-equivariance of X_w (3.26); similarly X^{□,w}_{D,M_•} and X^w_{D,M_•}. Then |X^{□,w}_{W⁺,F_•}| ≅ X̂_{w,x}, these morphisms are closed immersions, and S(x) := {w : x ∈ X_w(L)} = {w : X^w_{D,M_•} ≠ 0}.
items.note: The proof of Proposition 3.5.10 prints an object of X^□_{W⁺,F_•}(A) with an undefined entry "F_W" in place of the deformed filtration F_{A,•}; see source issue E9.

items.name: Each w-component is a normal domain
items.statement: For w ∈ S(x), X^{□,w}_{D,M_•} is pro-representable by a complete local normal domain of residue field L and dimension [K:Q_p](n² + n(n+1)/2), formally smooth over X̂_{w,x}. This is where the normality of X_w (Theorem 2.3.6) is used, together with the stability of normal domains under completion for excellent local rings.

items.name: The map Θ detects which component a deformation lies on
items.statement: The map (κ₁,κ₂) induces X̂_x → T̂_{(0,0)} and X̂_{w,x} → T̂_{w,(0,0)}, and Θ denotes the resulting morphism X_{D,M_•} → T̂_{(0,0)}, independent of the framing. For w ∈ S(x) and w′ ∈ S, the morphisms induced by Θ on X^{□,w}_{D,M_•} and on X^w_{D,M_•} factor through T̂_{w′,(0,0)} if and only if w′ = w.

items.name: The framed Galois deformation groupoid X_r
items.statement: For r : G_K → GL_n(L) continuous with associated representation V, X_r is the groupoid of deformations of r and X_V that of deformations of V; X_r → X_V is relatively representable and formally smooth of relative dimension n².
items.note: Split by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/2). This matches LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1 only by analogy: R08.1's nodes treat a residual ρ̄ over O, and the identification of X_r with the completion X̂_{r̄,r} is Kisin's [53, Lemma 2.3.3, Proposition 2.3.5], which no node states. The trianguline groupoids are item 3.6-trianguline-galois-groupoids.

items.name: Structure of the trianguline Galois deformation ring
items.statement: Assume V trianguline with a triangulation M_• admitting a locally algebraic parameter in T^n_0(L), W⁺ = B⁺_dR ⊗ V regular, and x ∈ X(L) as above. (i) |X_{r,M_•}| is pro-represented by a reduced equidimensional complete local ring R_{r,M_•} of dimension n² + [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2. (ii) For w ∈ S(x), |X^w_{r,M_•}| is pro-represented by R_{r,M_•}/p_w with p_w a minimal prime and the quotient normal, and w ↦ p_w is a bijection from S(x) onto the minimal primes of R_{r,M_•}. (iii) The composite of Θ with |X^w_{r,M_•}| factors through T̂_{w′,(0,0)} if and only if w′ = w.

items.name: Tangent-space dimension of the w-component
items.statement: For w ∈ S(x), dim_L X^w_{r,M_•}(L[ε]) = n² − [K:Q_p]n² + [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 + dim_L T_{X_w,x}.

items.name: The Bruhat constraint from the relative position of the two flags
items.statement: Let w_x ∈ S be the relative position of the pair of flags (α^{−1}(𝒟_•), α^{−1}(Fil_{W⁺,•})), independent of α. If w ∈ S(x), equivalently X^w_{r,M_•} ≠ 0, then w_x ≼ w.

items.name: The trianguline variety
items.statement: T_reg ⊂ T_L is the complement of the z^{−k} and ε(z)z^k with k ∈ Z^Σ_{≥0}, and T^n_reg the locus where δ_i/δ_j ∈ T_reg for i ≠ j; T^n_0 ⊊ T^n_reg. For r̄ : G_K → GL_n(k_L) with framed deformation ring R_r̄ and 𝔛_r̄ := (Spf R_r̄)^rig, the trianguline variety X_tri(r̄) is the Zariski closure in 𝔛_r̄ × T^n_L of U_tri(r̄) := {(r,δ) ∈ 𝔛_r̄ × T^n_reg : r is trianguline of parameter δ} (3.29). It is reduced and equidimensional of dimension n² + [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2, with U_tri(r̄) Zariski-open, and ω′ denotes the projection to T^n_L.
items.note: Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/2): missing, and built in route 2. LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3 plans Kisin's potentially semistable rings only, and PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.7, whose global triangulation Propositions 3.7.1–3.7.2 need, is not among R08.3's ancestors.

items.name: Uniqueness of the triangulation of a given generic parameter
items.statement: If δ ∈ T^n_0 then the (φ,Γ_K)-module M over R_{L,K}[1/t] has a unique triangulation of parameter δ.

items.name: The completed local ring of the trianguline variety embeds in the deformation groupoid
items.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism X_r ≅ 𝔛̂_{r̄,r} and hence a morphism X̂_tri(r̄)_x → X_r; it factors through X_{r,M_•} (Proposition 3.7.2, via the global triangulation of [49, Cor. 6.3.10] after a proper birational modification), and both X̂_tri(r̄)_x → X_{r,M_•} and X̂_tri(r̄)_x → X_r are closed immersions.

items.name: The weight permutation and the component reached by Θ
items.statement: For x = (r,δ) with δ locally algebraic and W⁺ regular, let h_{τ,1} < … < h_{τ,n} be the Sen weights of r and let w = (w_τ)_τ ∈ S be defined by wt_τ(δ_{w_τ(i)}) = h_{τ,i}. Then the composite Θ_x : X̂_tri(r̄)_x → T̂_{(0,0)} factors through T̂_{w,(0,0)}. The proof compares the two weight maps through the Sen polynomial: the graded comparison (3.31), the computation of the Sen polynomial of an almost de Rham lattice (Lemma 3.7.5), the Sen polynomial of the deformation (Lemma 3.7.6) and a root-matching lemma over a local ring (Lemma 3.7.7).
items.note: The first display in the proof of Lemma 3.7.4 prints "wt_τ(δ_i)_{τ∈Σ}" without the inner parentheses; see source issue E9.

items.name: The trianguline variety is a single component of the deformation ring
items.statement: The closed immersion X̂_tri(r̄)_x ↪ X_{r,M_•} induces an isomorphism X̂_tri(r̄)_x ≅ X^w_{r,M_•}, w being the weight permutation of Lemma 3.7.4.

items.name: The standing hypotheses on the point x, and their crystalline sufficient condition
items.statement: The assumptions on x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(r̄)(L) are: δ locally algebraic; δ_iδ_j^{−1} and εδ_iδ_j^{−1} not algebraic for i ≠ j; and the τ-Sen weights of the representation attached to r distinct for each τ. They hold whenever the representation is crystalline with distinct Hodge–Tate weights for each τ and the eigenvalues φ_i of φ^{[K_0:Q_p]} on D_cris satisfy φ_iφ_j^{−1} ∉ {1, p^{[K_0:Q_p]}} for i ≠ j.

items.name: The local model diagram
items.statement: For x = (r,δ) satisfying Remark 3.7.9 there is a commutative diagram (3.33) of formal schemes over L whose top row is X̂_tri(r̄)_x ≅ X^w_{r,M_•} ← X^{□,w}_{r,M_•} → X^{□,w}_{V,M_•} ≅ X^{□,w}_{D,M_•} → X^{□,w}_{W⁺,F_•} ≅ X̂_{w,x_pdR}, with middle and bottom rows the unframed and unfiltered analogues; every horizontal morphism which is not an isomorphism is formally smooth, every vertical morphism is a closed immersion and every square is cartesian. This is the local model theorem announced as Theorem 1.6.

items.name: Local normality and Cohen–Macaulayness of the trianguline variety
items.statement: Let x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(r̄) satisfy the assumptions of Remark 3.7.9. Then X_tri(r̄) is normal, hence irreducible, and Cohen–Macaulay at x. This follows from Theorem 3.6.2(ii), Proposition 2.3.3 and the diagram (3.33).

items.name: Flatness of the character map at such points
items.statement: For x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(r̄) satisfying Remark 3.7.9, the morphism ω′ : X_tri(r̄) → T^n_L is flat in a neighbourhood of x; the same then holds for the weight map ω to W^n_L. On the Zariski-open U_tri(r̄) the map ω′ is even smooth, but it can be ramified in general.
items.locator: Proposition 4.1.1 with the following paragraph, printed pp. 371–373

items.name: The accumulation property
items.statement: X_tri(r̄) satisfies the accumulation property at a point x with ω(x) algebraic and satisfying Remark 3.7.9: for every C > 0 the crystalline strictly dominant points with pairwise distinct Frobenius eigenvalues, non-critical, and with consecutive weight gaps greater than C accumulate at x.

items.name: Tangent space of the trianguline variety at a de Rham point
items.statement: Let x = (r,δ) satisfy Remark 3.7.9 with r de Rham, and let d_{w′} be the rank of the lattice generated by the w′(α) − α. Then (i) dim T_{X_tri(r̄),x} = dim X_tri(r̄) − [K:Q_p]n² + dim T_{X_w,x_pdR}, so X_tri(r̄) is smooth at x if and only if X_w is smooth at x_pdR; and (ii) dim T_{X_tri(r̄),x} ≤ dim X_tri(r̄) − d_{ww_x^{−1}} + lg(w_xw_0) + dim T_{Ū_w,π(x_pdR)} − [K:Q_p]n(n−1). In particular if π(x_pdR) is a smooth point of Ū_w and d_{ww_x^{−1}} = lg(w) − lg(w_x), then X_tri(r̄) is smooth at x.

items.name: The strictly dominant case and the comparison with the authors’ earlier bound
items.statement: When w = w_0 the smoothness hypothesis on π(x_pdR) is automatic and (4.1) dim T_{X_tri(r̄),x} ≤ dim X_tri(r̄) − d_{w_xw_0} + lg(w_xw_0), which is exactly the bound of [20, Th. 1.3] once one notes that the permutation w_x here is w_x^{old}w_0 in the notation of loc. cit. Both hypotheses of (ii) hold when lg(w) − lg(w_x) ≤ 2. Granting Conjecture 2.3.7 for w = w_0, (4.1) is an equality, which implies [20, Conj. 2.8].

items.name: Local companion points
items.statement: For x = (r,δ) with r de Rham with distinct Hodge–Tate weights h and wt(δ) = w_0(h) (strict dominance), a companion point of x is an x′ = (r,δ′) ∈ X_tri(r̄) with δ′_i/δ_i algebraic for every i; then wt(δ′) = w′(h) for some w′ ∈ S. When r is crystalline, a refinement φ is an ordering of the eigenvalues of φ^{[K_0:Q_p]} on D_cris(r), δ = z^{w_0(h)}unr(φ), and every companion point has the form (r, z^{w(h)}unr(φ)).
items.locator: Definition 4.2.1 with the surrounding text, printed p. 375
items.note: Two notational slips in this passage — a free index in the definition of z^h, and wt_τ where wt is meant; see source issue E10.

items.name: All local companion points in the crystalline case
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of §4.2 — r̄ fixed, x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(r̄) with r crystalline, Hodge–Tate weights distinct, δ = z^{w_0(h)}unr(φ) strictly dominant and φ_iφ_j^{−1} ∉ {1, p^{[K_0:Q_p]}} for i ≠ j — the set of companion points of x is exactly {x_w := (r, z^{w(h)}unr(φ)) : w_x ≼ w}. The necessity of w_x ≼ w comes from Corollary 3.7.8 and Proposition 3.6.4; the existence of every x_w with w ≽ w_x is proved by a Zariski-density argument inside the space of crystalline points, and does not use the local model. The paper presents this as the local analogue of [16, Conj. 6.6]. An analogue holds for r merely de Rham.

items.name: Cycles on the framed deformation ring and the two fibres
items.statement: For r ∈ 𝔛_r̄(L), Ô_{𝔛_r̄,r} represents the framed deformations of r and has dimension n² + [K:Q_p]n². X_tri(r̄)_δ is the fibre of ω′ at δ and X_tri(r̄)_{wt(δ)} the fibre of the weight map. Taking completions in (3.33) and then fibres over 0 ∈ t gives the diagram (4.6), whose components are indexed by the components of the Steinberg variety through x_pdR; one obtains cycles 𝖅_{w′} of codimension [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 and 𝕮_{w′} := Σ_{w″} a_{w′,w″}𝖅_{w″} (4.7), independent of the framing. Taking instead the fibre at δ gives (4.11) and cycles 𝒵_{w′}, 𝒞_{w′} of codimension [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 + n (4.12) (printed [K:Q_p]n(n+3)/2; E12).
items.note: The two families of cycles are distinguished in the printed text only by font; any formalisation must name them apart.

items.name: Identification of the top cycle with the crystalline deformation cycle
items.statement: If r is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights given by wt(δ) and δ ∈ T^n_0, then 𝕮_{w_0} = 𝖅_{w_0} corresponds to an irreducible closed subscheme of Spec Ô of the crystalline deformation space of dimension n² + [K:Q_p]n(n−1)/2, and since that space is already irreducible of this dimension, 𝕮_{w_0} ≅ [Spec Ô_{𝔛^{wt(δ)−cr}_r̄,r}] (4.8). Moreover r is de Rham if and only if 𝖅_{w_0} ≠ 0.

items.name: The weight fibre as a Kazhdan–Lusztig combination
items.statement: For x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(r̄)(L) with the unique triangulation of parameter δ and w with wt(δ) = w(h), [Spec Ô_{X_tri(r̄)_{wt(δ)},x}] = Σ_{w′∈S} P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1)𝕮_{w′}. More precisely the sum runs over w_{x_pdR} ≼ w′ ≼ w (4.9), and when r is de Rham every term is non-zero.
items.note: The statement of Corollary 4.3.2 is printed with a broken clause ("Let M_• be … and that w ∈ S is such that …"); see source issue E10.

items.name: The locally analytic Breuil–Mézard type conjecture
items.statement: CONJECTURE (Conjecture 4.3.4, not proved in general). For every generic trianguline r ∈ 𝔛_r̄(L) and every absolutely irreducible constituent Π of a locally Q_p-analytic principal series of GL_n(K), there is a unique cycle C_{r,Π} of codimension [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 + n in Z(Spec Ô_{𝔛_r̄,r}) with [Spec Ô_{X_tri(r̄)_δ,(r,δ)}] = Σ_Π m_{δ,Π}C_{r,Π} for every δ, the left-hand side being 0 when (r,δ) ∉ X_tri(r̄). It implies that the fibre is equidimensional of dimension n² − n + [K:Q_p]n(n−1)/2 when non-zero (printed codimension [K:Q_p]n(n+3)/2 and dimension n² + [K:Q_p]n(n−3)/2; E12), and determines which (r,δ) lie on X_tri(r̄).
items.note: A conjecture; only uniqueness (Proposition 4.3.6) and the generic crystalline case (Theorem 4.3.8) are proved.

items.name: Uniqueness of the cycles
items.statement: For r generic trianguline with integral τ-Sen weights, the cycles C_{r,Π} of Conjecture 4.3.4, if they exist, are unique. The proof uses that a point of X_tri(r̄) has locally algebraic parameter in T^n_0, that each constituent occurs with multiplicity one in a suitable principal series, and descending induction along the strong linkage order.
items.locator: Proposition 4.3.6 with the preceding description of the constituents, printed pp. 381–382

items.name: The cycle depends only on r and the constituent
items.statement: With the notation of (4.12), the cycle 𝒞_{w′} depends only on r and on the constituent Π_{w′}, not on the chosen triangulation. The proof uses that the components of the Steinberg variety occurring in the characteristic cycle are stabilised by the parabolic P_{w′} (Remark 2.4.9) together with Lemma 3.4.7.
items.note: Its cycles are those of item 4.3-cycles-setup, whose codimension is corrected by E12 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/4).

items.name: The conjecture holds for generic crystalline r
items.statement: Assume r ∈ 𝔛_r̄(L) is generic crystalline with distinct τ-Sen weights for every τ — equivalently crystalline with distinct Hodge–Tate weights and φ_iφ_j^{−1} ∉ {1, p^{[K_0:Q_p]}} for i ≠ j. Then Conjecture 4.3.4 holds for r, with C_{r,Π_{w′}} := 𝒞_{w′}; the consistency across different characters uses Theorem 4.2.3, and the final identity [Spec Ô_{X_tri(r̄)_δ,(r,δ)}] = Σ_{w′} P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1)𝒞_{w′} matches the multiplicities m_{δ,Π_{w′}} = P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1). The constituents that occur are exactly the companion constituents of [15, §6].
items.note: Its cycles are those of item 4.3-cycles-setup, whose codimension is corrected by E12 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/4).

items.name: The global setting of §5
items.statement: Assume p > 2. F⁺ is totally real, F a totally imaginary quadratic extension splitting at all places above p, G a unitary group in n ≥ 2 variables over F⁺ with G ×_{F⁺} F ≅ GL_{n/F}, G(F⁺⊗_Q R) compact and G quasi-split at every finite place of F⁺. For each v ∈ S_p a place ṽ of F above v is fixed, giving i_ṽ : G(F⁺_v) ≅ GL_n(F_ṽ); K_v, B_v, B̄_v, T_v are the preimages of the integral, upper triangular, lower triangular and diagonal subgroups, and L is large enough to split every F⁺_v.

items.name: Completed cohomology, its Hecke algebra and localisation
items.statement: For a tame level U^p, Ŝ(U^p,L) is the Banach space of continuous functions G(F⁺)\G(A^∞_{F⁺})/U^p → L with the unitary G_p-action. S is a finite set of finite places split in F containing S_p and the places where U_v is not maximal, T^S the spherical Hecke algebra, and m^S a maximal ideal with Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S} ≠ 0; ρ̄ is the associated absolutely semisimple Galois representation, assumed absolutely irreducible.
items.note: The localised completed cohomology is printed as an inverse limit of O_L/m^s-valued functions, i.e. an O_L-module, where the L-Banach space is meant; see source issue E11. Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/5). CompletedCohomologyPartII owns completed cohomology in arbitrary reductive-group dimension: CC.1 the tame Hecke operators, CC.2 completion, CC.5 admissibility, CC.8 the unitary tower models, tame Hecke actions and localisation at a residual Hecke ideal. R31.2 plans locally algebraic vectors for GL₂/ℚ and imports all this from CC. The very strongly admissible locally analytic vectors are item 5.1-locally-analytic-vectors, and R_{ρ̄,S} is item 5.1-deformation-ring.

items.name: The Hecke eigenvariety and the map to the trianguline varieties
items.statement: Y(U^p,ρ̄) is the schematic support of the coherent sheaf (J_{B_p}(Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S}))^∨ on X_{ρ̄,S} × T̂_{p,L}, with J_{B_p} Emerton’s Jacquet functor: a reduced rigid variety of dimension n[F⁺:Q], closed in X_{ρ̄,S} × T̂_{p,L}, whose points are the (ρ,δ) with a non-zero Hom from δ into the Jacquet module. With the twist ι_v(δ_1,…,δ_n) := δ_{B_v}·(δ_1, δ_2ε, …, δ_nε^{n−1}) (5.1) there is a morphism Y(U^p,ρ̄) → X_tri(ρ̄_p) = ∏_{v∈S_p} X_tri(ρ̄_ṽ) (5.2).
items.note: Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/7). A definite-unitary finite-slope eigenvariety is planned at AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.3, on PadicFamilies L2a, with rigid character and weight spaces from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0a (the torus T̂_{p,L} adds a G_m-type factor for the uniformiser). What this item needs is Emerton's Jacquet-module construction of Y(U^p,ρ̄), which also defines the patched eigenvariety and gives the point criterion of §§5.3–5.4; it imports Emerton's Jacquet functor (item 5.2-emerton-jacquet) and is compared with AG2.3's eigenvariety wherever the two are identified.

items.name: De Rham and crystalline strictly dominant points, and classicality
items.statement: x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) is de Rham (resp. crystalline) strictly dominant if every ρ_ṽ is de Rham (resp. crystalline) and the image of x in each X_tri(ρ̄_ṽ) is strictly dominant, equivalently wt_τ(δ_{v,i}) ≥ wt_τ(δ_{v,i+1}) for all i, τ, v. With F^{G_p}_{B̄_p}(δ) the Orlik–Strauch representation (5.3) and LA(δ) its maximal locally algebraic quotient (5.4), membership in Y(U^p,ρ̄) is equivalent to a non-zero Hom from F^{G_p}_{B̄_p}(δ) (5.5), and x is classical when such a morphism factors through LA(δ), equivalently when ρ comes from a classical automorphic representation.

items.name: The classicality conjecture
items.statement: CONJECTURE (Conjecture 5.1.1). Every de Rham strictly dominant point of Y(U^p,ρ̄) is classical.
items.note: A conjecture; Theorem 5.1.3 proves the generic crystalline case.

items.name: Classicality of generic crystalline strictly dominant points
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ unramified, ᵖ√1 ∉ F, U_v hyperspecial at the places inert in F and ρ̄(G_{F(ᵖ√1)}) adequate. Let x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) be crystalline strictly dominant with φ_{ṽ,i}φ_{ṽ,j}^{−1} ∉ {1, q_v} for i ≠ j and v ∈ S_p. Then x is classical. The proof passes to the patched eigenvariety and uses Corollary 3.7.10 at each place: local irreducibility supplies the unique component through the image of x, which is exactly the hypothesis of the classicality criterion of [20, Th. 3.9].

items.name: Automorphy without strict dominance
items.statement: If x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) satisfies the hypotheses of Theorem 5.1.3 but is not strictly dominant, there is a strictly dominant x′ = (ρ,δ′) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄), which is classical by Theorem 5.1.3; hence ρ is automorphic, although x itself need not be classical. Under the same hypotheses the crystalline assumption should be relaxable to crystabelline genericity.

items.name: The patched eigenvariety and its component decomposition
items.statement: With R_∞ the maximal reduced Z_p-flat quotient of (⊗̂_{v∈S}R_{ρ̄_ṽ})[[x_1,…,x_g]] and X_∞ = X_{ρ̄^p} × X_{ρ̄_p} × U^g, the patched representation Π_∞ of [23] and the ideal a with Π_∞[a] ≅ Ŝ(U^p,L)_{m^S} give the patched eigenvariety X_p(ρ̄), the support of (J_{B_p}(Π_∞^{R_∞−an}))^∨ (5.7); Y(U^p,ρ̄) is the closed subspace cut out by a. For each irreducible component X^p of X_{ρ̄^p} there is a union X^{X^p−aut}_tri(ρ̄_p) of components of X_tri(ρ̄_p) with X_p(ρ̄) ≅ ⋃_{X^p}(X^p × ι(X^{X^p−aut}_tri(ρ̄_p)) × U^g) (5.8).
items.note: Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/6): missing. R31.5 plans the patched completed module for GL₂/ℚ, not a GL_n patched module, a patched eigenvariety or Emerton's Jacquet functor, and no trianguline or Jacquet stage is upstream of it, so (5.8) cannot be proved there. This item keeps the patched eigenvariety X_p(ρ̄) and its decomposition (5.8); the patched module is item 5.1-patched-module. Routed to route 3.

items.name: The adjunction between Orlik–Strauch induction and Lie-algebra homomorphisms
items.statement: For Π^an very strongly admissible, M in category O and V a smooth representation of T_p, Hom_{G_p}(F^{G_p}_{B̄_p}(Hom(M,L)^{ū∞}, V(δ_{B_p}^{−1})), Π^an) ≅ Hom_{T_p⁺}(V, Hom_{U(g)}(M,Π^an)^{U_0}) functorially in M, where Hom_{U(g)}(M,Π^an)^{U_0} carries the Hecke action (5.9). Specialised to irreducible constituents and to Verma modules this gives Hom_{G_p}(F^{G_p}_{B̄_p}(L̄(−ν), 1[s]_smε_smδ_{B_p}^{−1}), Π^an) ≅ Hom_{U(g)}(L(ν),Π^an)^{U_0}[m^s_{ε_sm}] and the analogous statement for U(g)⊗_{U(b)}μ, the latter space being finite dimensional.
items.note: It is stated for any very strongly admissible Π^an (p. 390), and so are Lemmas 5.2.4–5.2.6; the Part II proves them in that general form, importing the Orlik–Strauch functor and Emerton's adjunction from route 6 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/8).

items.name: Finite dimensionality for an arbitrary object of category O
items.statement: For any object M of category O and any s ≥ 1, Hom_{U(g)}(M, Π^an)^{U_0}[m^s_{ε_sm}] is finite dimensional. This follows from the Verma case together with left exactness, the fact that every simple object of O is a quotient of a Verma module, and finite length in O.
items.note: Lemma 5.2.4 is printed as a verbatim repetition of the first assertion of Lemma 5.2.3, i.e. for the Verma module rather than for an arbitrary M; its proof gives the statement recorded here. See source issue E4.

items.name: Exactness criteria for the Hom functor on category O
items.statement: If the continuous dual Π′ is a finite projective O_L[[K_p]][1/p]-module then M ↦ Hom_{U(g)}(M,Π^an) is exact on finite type U(g)-modules (Lemma 5.2.5). Assuming that exactness (5.10) and that Π^an is the locally analytic vectors of a continuous admissible representation, the functor Hom_{U(g)}(−,Π^an)^{U_0}[m^∞_{ε_sm}] is exact on category O (Lemma 5.2.6).

items.name: A combinatorial lemma on the Bruhat order
items.statement: If lg(w) ≤ lg(w_0) − 2 there are exactly two elements w_1, w_2 with w ≼ w_i ≼ w_3, lg(w_i) = lg(w)+1 and lg(w_3) = lg(w)+2 for a third element w_3.

items.name: Refinements, companion characters and the permutation w_R
items.statement: Fix ρ ∈ X_{ρ̄,S} coming from a classical point of Y(U^p,ρ̄), with Hodge–Tate weights h_{ṽ,τ,1} < … < h_{ṽ,τ,n} and λ defined by λ_{v,τ,i} = h_{ṽ,τ,n+1−i} + i − 1, and assume each ρ_ṽ crystabelline generic, i.e. the Weil-group representation ⊕_i η_{ṽ,i} attached to ρ_ṽ satisfies (η_{ṽ,i}^{−1}η_{ṽ,j})∘rec ∉ {1, |·|} for i ≠ j. A refinement R orders the η_{ṽ,i} at each place; δ_{R,w} is the associated character (5.13), with derivative ww_0·λ and smooth part independent of w, and R ↦ (ρ,δ_{R,w_0}) is a bijection between refinements and classical points of Y(U^p,ρ̄) of the form (ρ,δ). w_R is the permutation attached to the image of (ρ,δ_{R,w_0}) in the trianguline varieties.

items.name: The companion constituent conjecture
items.statement: CONJECTURE (Conjecture 5.3.1, a case of [16, Conj. 6.1]). For a refinement R and w ∈ ∏_{v∈S_p}S_n^{[F_ṽ:Q_p]}, Hom_{G_p}(F^{G_p}_{B̄_p}(L̄(−ww_0·λ), δ_{R,sm}δ_{B_p}^{−1}), Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S}[m_ρ]) ≠ 0 if and only if w_R ≼ w. It is stronger than predicting the companion points of x, since it also determines which (ρ, z^μδ_{R,sm}) lie on the eigenvariety.

items.name: All expected companion constituents exist in the crystalline case
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ unramified, ᵖ√1 ∉ F, U^p small enough with U_v hyperspecial at the inert places and ρ̄(G_{F(ᵖ√1)}) adequate. Let ρ ∈ X_{ρ̄,S} come from a classical point of Y(U^p,ρ̄) with every ρ_ṽ crystalline and φ_{ṽ,i}φ_{ṽ,j}^{−1} ∉ {1, q_v} for i ≠ j and v ∈ S_p. Then Conjecture 5.3.1 holds for ρ. The necessity of w_R ≼ w comes from Theorem 4.2.3; the existence is a descending induction on the length, run on the patched eigenvariety, whose inductive step compares two cycle identities.

items.name: The two cycle identities of the induction
items.statement: For a suitable point y of the patched space with Weyl element w_y, writing L(w′w_0·μ) for the dual of Hom_{U(g)}(L(w′w_0·μ), Π^an_∞[m^∞_{r_y}])^{U_0}[m^∞_{ε_{w,sm}}] and M(ww_0·μ) for the pull-back of M_∞ to the weight fibre, one has in Z^d(Spec Ô_{X_∞,r_y}) with d = [F⁺:Q]n(n+1)/2: [M(ww_0·μ)] = Σ_{w_y ≼ w′ ≼ w} P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1)[L(w′w_0·μ)] (5.23) and [Ô_{X_p(ρ̄)_{ww_0·μ},y_w}] = Σ_{w_y ≼ w′ ≼ w} P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1)C_{w′} (5.24), where C_{w′} is the pull-back of the product over v ∈ S_p of the local cycles of §4.3 and is non-zero in that range. The induction hypothesis also asserts that the rank of M_∞ near each companion point y_w is the same integer m_y.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.3.3, Steps 3–6, formulas (5.23)–(5.24), printed pp. 397–400
items.note: The Claim of Step 3 is printed with the condition "w_R ≼ w", but w_R is defined only for a refinement of the fixed global ρ while y is a general point; the induction proves it with w_y ≼ w. See source issue E3.

items.name: Expected strengthenings of the companion theorem
items.statement: The authors expect that the crystalline hypothesis can be dropped, keeping crystabelline genericity, and that under the same hypotheses every irreducible locally Q_p-analytic subquotient C of a principal series with Hom_{G_p}(C, Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S}[m_ρ]) ≠ 0 is one of the constituents of (5.12) for some refinement and some w ≽ w_R. Special cases were known before: GL_2(Q_p) for completed H¹ of modular curves, Ding’s results for n = 2, and partial results for GL_n(Q_p).
items.note: Expectations, not theorems. The printed text of (i) writes the ideal as p_ρ, which is never defined; see source issue E11.

items.name: The eigenvariety is locally the fibre of the patched eigenvariety
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 5.1.3, the map Y(U^p,ρ̄) → X_p(ρ̄) ×_{(Spf S_∞)^rig} Sp L (5.38) is an isomorphism of rigid spaces in a neighbourhood of a crystalline strictly dominant x with generic Frobenius eigenvalues; in particular that fibre product is reduced at such a point. The proof notes that Ô_{X_p(ρ̄),x} is the completed local ring of X_{ρ̄^p} × ι(X_tri(ρ̄_p)) × U^g by Corollary 3.7.10, so X_p(ρ̄) is Cohen–Macaulay at x, and records that the argument of [19, Th. 4.8] needs that Cohen–Macaulayness, which was overlooked in the proof of [20, Cor. 5.18].
items.note: The parenthesis of this proof is the authors’ own correction to their earlier paper [20]; recorded in the report and the errata log rather than as a source issue of this paper.

items.name: Cohen–Macaulayness, flatness of the weight map, and singularity
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ unramified, ᵖ√1 ∉ F, U^p small enough with U_v hyperspecial at the inert places and ρ̄(G_{F(ᵖ√1)}) adequate. Let x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) be crystalline strictly dominant with φ_{ṽ,i}φ_{ṽ,j}^{−1} ∉ {1, q_v} for i ≠ j and v ∈ S_p. Then Y(U^p,ρ̄) is Cohen–Macaulay at x and the weight map Y(U^p,ρ̄) → T̂^0_{p,L} is flat at x; and if w_xw_0 is not a product of distinct simple reflections then Y(U^p,ρ̄) is singular at x. The singularity comes from the tangent-space computation dim T_{X_tri(ρ̄_p),x_p} = lg(w_xw_0) − d_{w_xw_0} + dim X_tri(ρ̄_p) (5.39) together with the fact that d_w < lg(w) exactly when w is not such a product.

items.name: What is left open at the companion points
items.statement: The same argument shows that if X_p(ρ̄) is singular at a companion point x_w then so is Y(U^p,ρ̄); which companion points are singular for w ≠ w_0 is left open and is related to Conjecture 2.3.7. Equality (5.39) shows that the tangent-space dimension of X_tri(ρ̄_ṽ) at the image of x is as predicted by [20, Conj. 2.8], so that conjecture holds at many points. When w_xw_0 is a product of distinct simple reflections, work of Bergdall leads one to expect that Y(U^p,ρ̄) is smooth at x; the method of this paper gives no information there.

items.name: The BGG category O and its block O(0)
items.statement: O is the BGG category of finitely generated U(g)-modules attached to g ⊃ b ⊃ t that are t-semisimple and locally U(b)-finite; O(0) is its block of the trivial infinitesimal character, containing the M(ww_0·0) and L(ww_0·0) for w ∈ W.
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/1). Planned nowhere: LieHighestWeight excludes full category O. Routed to the LieHighestWeight Part II of PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-25 route 3 (route 8), which plans algebraic category O but no Kazhdan–Lusztig theory.

items.name: Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials of the Weyl group
items.statement: The Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials P_{x,y} ∈ Z[q] of the Weyl group W, with P_{x,y} ≠ 0 if and only if x ≼ y in the Bruhat order, and P_{x,x} = 1.
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/1). Routed to route 8.

items.name: The Kazhdan–Lusztig multiplicity theorem
items.statement: For w, w′ ∈ W, [M(ww_0·0) : L(w′w_0·0)] = P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1); hence L(w′w_0·0) occurs in M(ww_0·0) if and only if w′ ≼ w (the Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture, proved by Beilinson–Bernstein 1981 and Brylinski–Kashiwara 1981; Humphreys §8.4).
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/1). Theorem 2.4.7(ii), Corollary 2.5.6, Corollary 4.3.2 (4.9), Theorem 4.3.8 and the cycle identities (1.2)–(1.3) and (5.23)–(5.24) rest on it. No stage plans it; routed to route 8 as a stated input. Its proof by localisation needs the D-module foundations and Beilinson–Bernstein localisation that route 1 builds (items 2.4-dmodules, 2.4-BB), so the design jobs must order those layers before it, or keep the theorem as a stated input.

items.name: D-module foundations: coherent, holonomic and regular holonomic D-modules and characteristic cycles
items.statement: For a smooth variety Y over a field of characteristic 0: coherent D_Y-modules, good filtrations, the characteristic variety and characteristic cycle ([44, Cor. 2.3.2]); holonomic and regular holonomic D-modules, and G-equivariant ones on G/B × G/B, as used for the Beilinson–Bernstein equivalence and the characteristic cycles of §2.4.
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/1). No stage plans D-modules; route 1 builds them, together with Beilinson–Bernstein localisation on G/B (item 2.4-BB) and characteristic cycles (item 2.4.4-char-cycles).

items.name: The flag variety G/B and the G-orbits on G/B × G/B
items.statement: G/B is a smooth projective k-scheme. G acts diagonally on G/B ×_k G/B, and for w ∈ W with a lift ẇ, U_w := G·(1, ẇ)B × B is a locally closed subscheme, smooth of dimension dim G − dim B + lg(w), with G/B × G/B = ∐_w U_w; its closure is Ū_w = ∐_{w′≼w} U_{w′}. The smooth locus of Ū_w is the notion used in Theorem 2.4.7(iii).
items.locator: §2.1, printed p. 310; used in Theorem 2.4.7(iii), Proposition 2.5.3 and Proposition 4.1.5
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/9). No stage plans G/B as a scheme or the orbit geometry: ReductiveGroups Layer 7 plans the group theory only. Routed with its consumer (route 1), as the verifier allows; a Part II of Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups, joining DESIGN-ReductiveGroupsPartIII (ShimuraData D3 builds flag varieties too), is the alternative for the maintainer.

items.name: The trianguline Galois deformation groupoids
items.statement: D_rig induces X_V ≅ X_D for D := D_rig(V). For V trianguline with a triangulation M_• of M := D[1/t], X_{V,M_•} := X_V ×_{X_D} X_{D,M_•} and X_{r,M_•} := X_r ×_{X_V} X_{V,M_•}, with framed versions; the framing □ is on D_pdR(B_dR ⊗ V), not directly on the Galois deformation, and all automorphisms in these groupoids are trivial.
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/2), split from item 3.6-galois-groupoids: not planned at R08.1. Routed to route 2.

items.name: B-pairs and Berger's equivalence, with coefficients
items.statement: A B-pair is (W_e, W⁺_dR) with W_e a B_e-representation of G_K, B_e = B_cris^{φ=1}, and W⁺_dR a G_K-stable B⁺_dR-lattice in B_dR ⊗_{B_e} W_e. Berger's theorem gives an equivalence between (φ,Γ_K)-modules over R_K and B-pairs; with coefficients in A, M ↦ W_e(M) is a rank-preserving equivalence between ΦΓ_{A,K} and A⊗_{Q_p}B_e-representations of G_K, with quasi-inverse W_e ↦ D(W_e, W⁺_dR)[1/t].
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.5.1, printed p. 355 (citing Berger, Construction de (φ,Γ)-modules, Algebra & Number Theory 2 (2008))
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/3), taken out of item 3.5.1-fibre-product. PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18 routes B-pairs (its items 886, 1104) to the same PadicHodgeTheory Part II; routed there (route 4).

items.name: The polarized global deformation ring R_{ρ̄,S}
items.statement: R_{ρ̄,S} pro-represents the deformations of ρ̄ unramified outside S satisfying ρ^∨∘c ≅ ρ ⊗ ε^{n−1}.
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/5), split from item 5.1-completed-cohomology.

items.name: Very strongly admissible locally analytic vectors
items.statement: For an admissible unitary Banach representation Π of G_p over L (here Ŝ(U^p,L)_{m^S}), the subspace Π^an of locally Q_p-analytic vectors is a very strongly admissible locally Q_p-analytic representation.
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/5), split from item 5.1-completed-cohomology. Planned by no stage; routed with the locally analytic representation theory (route 6).

items.name: The patched module of Caraiani–Emerton–Gee–Geraghty–Paškūnas–Shin for GL_n
items.statement: R_∞ is the maximal reduced Z_p-flat quotient of (⊗̂_{v∈S} R_{ρ̄_ṽ})[[x_1,…,x_g]], and the patched R_∞-module M_∞ carries the unitary G_p-representation Π_∞ of [23] for GL_n over the p-adic places of F, with an ideal a of R_∞ such that Π_∞[a] ≅ Ŝ(U^p,L)_{m^S}.
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/6), split from item 5.1-patched. PAPER-BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23 records the CEGGPS patched module as missing (its items 133–134) on its route 7, a Part II of the same parent, and the queue groups both into one design (issue #3459). Routed to route 3.

items.name: The Orlik–Strauch functor
items.statement: For G split reductive over K with L splitting K, a parabolic P with Levi M_P, an object M of the parabolic category O and a smooth admissible representation V of M_P, the Orlik–Strauch functor gives a locally Q_p-analytic representation F^G_{P̄}(M, V) of G; in §5 it is applied to Verma modules and their simple quotients with P the Borel ((5.3)).
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/8). PAPER-DING-25's new roadmap LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups owns the Orlik–Strauch functors (its brief (ii)); routed there (route 6).

items.name: The Orlik–Strauch irreducibility and Jordan–Hölder theorem
items.statement: The Orlik–Strauch description of when F^G_{P̄}(M, V) is irreducible and of the Jordan–Hölder constituents of locally analytic principal series, in the form used for the multiplicities m_{δ,Π} of Conjecture 4.3.4 and Theorem 4.3.8 and for 'each constituent occurs with multiplicity one' in Proposition 4.3.6.
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/8). Owned by LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (PAPER-DING-25's brief (ii)); routed there (route 6).

items.name: Emerton's locally analytic Jacquet functor
items.statement: Emerton's locally Q_p-analytic Jacquet functor J_B with respect to a Borel subgroup, from essentially admissible locally analytic representations of G to essentially admissible locally analytic representations of the torus T, so that the continuous dual of J_B(Π) is a coherent sheaf on the character space T̂; Y(U^p,ρ̄) and X_p(ρ̄) are schematic supports of such duals.
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/8). Owned by LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (PAPER-DING-25's brief (iii)); routed there (route 6).

items.name: Emerton's adjunction for the Jacquet functor
items.statement: Emerton's adjunction theorem relating G-equivariant maps from locally analytic parabolic inductions into a very strongly admissible locally analytic representation Π with (balanced) T-equivariant maps into J_B(Π) (Emerton, Jacquet modules of locally analytic representations of p-adic reductive groups II: the relation to parabolic induction), in the generalisation to Orlik–Strauch representations through which Lemma 5.2.1 uses it (Breuil [16]).

routes.title: The Grothendieck simultaneous resolution, the Steinberg variety and characteristic cycles
routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas plans this geometry: no stage mentions the Springer or Grothendieck simultaneous resolution, the Steinberg variety or the nilpotent cone, and the nearest neighbours — EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.2 for perverse sheaves and Hitchin geometry, GeometricSatakeAndFusion for the Fargues–Fontaine curve — own quite different objects. The Tau Ceti roadmaps own some inputs: Verma modules and L(λ) (LieHighestWeight Layer 3), and Borel subgroups, the Weyl group and the Bruhat decomposition (ReductiveGroups Layer 7, with quotients in Layer 3), recorded as `planned` imports. They do not own category O or Kazhdan–Lusztig theory, which go to the LieHighestWeight Part II of route 8, nor the flag variety G/B as a scheme with its orbit geometry, nor D-modules, which are built here (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/1, /9). A new roadmap is therefore the only route left, and the material justifies one: it is a self-contained piece of geometric representation theory used far beyond this paper.
routes.brief: Start from the flag variety G/B as a smooth projective scheme, the G-orbits U_w on G/B × G/B and their closures (item 2.1-flag-variety), importing Borel subgroups, the Weyl group and the Bruhat decomposition from Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 7. Build, over a field of good characteristic, the variety g̃ = {(gB,ψ) : Ad(g⁻¹)ψ ∈ b} as a vector bundle over G/B and Grothendieck’s simultaneous resolution q : g̃ → g, with its properness, quasi-finiteness over the regular locus and étale degree |W| over the regular semisimple locus. Construct X = g̃ ×_g g̃ with its projections π, κ₁, κ₂, prove that V_w → U_w is a vector bundle, that X is a reduced local complete intersection whose irreducible components are the X_w, and that each projection restricts to a proper birational map X_w → g̃ which is an isomorphism over the regular locus. Prove the fibres of κ_i are equidimensional, deduce flatness by miracle flatness, and import Bezrukavnikov–Riche for Cohen–Macaulayness, including the passage from characteristic p > h to characteristic zero by spreading out. Then prove **normality of the X_w** (Theorem 2.3.6 of the paper, which the authors believe to be new) by Serre’s criterion, via the analysis of the codimension-one strata; this is the property the trianguline-variety roadmap consumes. Construct the Steinberg variety and its components, the group of top-dimensional cycles, the Beilinson–Bernstein equivalence onto regular holonomic G-equivariant D-modules on G/B × G/B, characteristic cycles and their additivity, and prove that the three families of classes form bases of Z⁰(Z) with the Kazhdan–Lusztig transition matrix. Record Conjecture 2.3.7 and the failure of the Kazhdan–Lusztig irreducibility conjecture for SL_n with n ≥ 8 as facts about the landscape, never as targets. Build the D-module foundations used in §2.4 (coherent D-modules, good filtrations, characteristic varieties and cycles, holonomic and regular holonomic G-equivariant D-modules; item 2.4-dmodules) with Beilinson–Bernstein localisation on G/B. Import Verma modules and L(λ) from Tau Ceti LieHighestWeight Layer 3, and category O, its block O(0), the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials and the Kazhdan–Lusztig multiplicity theorem (a stated imported input, Beilinson–Bernstein and Brylinski–Kashiwara 1981) from the LieHighestWeight Part II of route 8, ordering the D-module layers before the layers that use that theorem, and export the tangent-space bound of Proposition 2.5.3 and the completed cycle identities of §2.5, which are what the p-adic side actually uses.

routes.title: The trianguline variety and its local model
routes.reason: The trianguline variety is not planned anywhere in the atlas: the word "trianguline" occurs only as an adjective in hypotheses of CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility (Emerton’s local–global compatibility, the Kisin conjecture in the trianguline case) and in a GL₂(Q_p) block check, never as the geometric object X_tri(r̄). Its ambient space and its coefficients do have owners, which this roadmap imports rather than rebuilds: the Robba ring and (φ,Γ_K)-modules from PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.0–RD.1, B_dR from PadicHodgeTheory R06.1, Sen theory from P7 (P7/sen-module), almost de Rham theory, B-pairs and Berger's functors from the PadicHodgeTheory Part II (route 4), and the framed local deformation ring from LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1. The trianguline variety itself is built here: it was marked planned at R08.3, which plans only Kisin's potentially semistable rings (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/2, /3). What is new here is the comparison itself, so it needs its own roadmap rather than a Part II of any of those.
routes.brief: Import from the PadicHodgeTheory Part II (route 4) almost de Rham B_dR-representations, B_pdR and D_pdR, Fontaine’s equivalence W ↦ (D_pdR(W), ν_W) with Rep_K(G_a) and its coefficient version over an artinian base, B-pairs with Berger's equivalence, and Berger's W⁺_dR and W_dR with coefficients. Construct the bijection between Galois-stable B⁺_dR-lattices and filtrations of D_pdR(W), whose graded pieces are finite projective over A⊗_{Q_p}K (E8), and prove that regular lattices give complete flags. Build the deformation groupoids X_W, X_{W,F_•}, X_{W⁺} and their framed versions and identify them with the completions of g, g̃ and X at the point given by the two flags and the nilpotent operator — this is where the geometry of SpringerResolutionAndCharacteristicCycles enters. On the (φ,Γ_K) side, construct trianguline modules, triangulations and parameters, the character space T and the genericity locus T^n_0 (defined by "δ_iδ_j⁻¹ **or** εδ_iδ_j⁻¹ algebraic for **some** i ≠ j" — the printed text has "and … for i ≠ j", which would make T^n_0 everything; see sourceIssue E2), the (φ,γ_K)-cohomology and its comparison with Galois cohomology, and prove the key formal smoothness theorem 3.4.4. Construct the trianguline variety X_tri(r̄) ⊂ 𝔛_r̄ × T^n_L as the Zariski closure (3.29) of U_tri(r̄) over T^n_reg, and prove, following Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen, Math. Ann. 367 (2017), Th. 2.6, that it is reduced and equidimensional of dimension n² + [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 with U_tri(r̄) Zariski-open. Import the framed ring R_r̄ from LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1 (the identification of X_r with the completion of 𝔛_r̄ at r is Kisin's Lemma 2.3.3 and Proposition 2.3.5, which no node states), the global triangulation of Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao from PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.7, the character space T^n_L from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0a, and the rigid generic fibre (Spf R_r̄)^rig from the adic-spaces roadmaps. Build the trianguline Galois deformation groupoids X_{V,M_•}, X_{r,M_•} and X_V ≅ X_D (item 3.6-trianguline-galois-groupoids). Then prove the structure theorem for the trianguline Galois deformation ring — reduced, equidimensional, with minimal primes in bijection with the Weyl-group elements w with x ∈ X_w — assemble the local model diagram (3.33), and deduce that the trianguline variety is normal, irreducible and Cohen–Macaulay at the points of Remark 3.7.9. Finally develop the local applications: flatness of the character and weight maps, the accumulation property, the tangent-space bound, the determination of all local companion points in the crystalline case, and the cycle formalism of §4.3 with the locally analytic Breuil–Mézard conjecture. The cycles of the character fibre have codimension [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 + n, not the printed [K:Q_p]n(n+3)/2, and that fibre has dimension n² − n + [K:Q_p]n(n−1)/2 (E12). Keep Conjecture 4.3.4 and Conjecture 2.3.7 as conjectures, and keep the two families of cycles of §4.3 — those of the weight fibre and those of the full character fibre — under distinct names, since the printed text distinguishes them only by font.

routes.title: Completed cohomology and p-adic local–global compatibility, Part II: eigenvarieties, classicality and companion constituents
routes.reason: Completed cohomology in arbitrary reductive-group dimension, with unitary tower models, tame Hecke actions and localisation, is owned by CompletedCohomologyPartII (CC.1, CC.2, CC.5, CC.8), which the parent imports; the parent's own stages are written for GL₂ over Q. A definite-unitary eigenvariety is planned at AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.3 on PadicFamilies L2a. What is new here is Emerton's Jacquet-module construction of Y(U^p,ρ̄) and of the patched eigenvariety X_p(ρ̄), the CEGGPS patched module for GL_n (beside PAPER-BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23's route 7 in the same Part II), and companion constituents (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/5–/7). This is the natural extension of that roadmap rather than a new one, and it consumes the local results through the map Y(U^p,ρ̄) → ∏_v X_tri(ρ̄_ṽ), so it must import TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel rather than repeat it.
routes.brief: Extend the parent from modular and Shimura curves to a definite unitary group G over a totally real field, split by a CM quadratic extension at the places above p and compact at infinity. Import completed cohomology, its Hecke action and localisation from CompletedCohomologyPartII (CC.1, CC.2, CC.5, CC.8), the deformation ring R_{ρ̄,S} from GlobalGaloisDeformations G7, very strongly admissible locally analytic vectors, the Orlik–Strauch functor and Emerton's Jacquet functor and adjunction from LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (route 6), and the trianguline variety from TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel (route 2). A definite-unitary eigenvariety is planned at AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.3 on PadicFamilies L2a, with weights from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0a (T̂_{p,L} adds a G_m-type factor for the uniformiser): plan only Emerton's Jacquet-module construction of Y(U^p,ρ̄) and the properties of §5.1 it needs, with a comparison to AG2.3's eigenvariety wherever the two are identified. Construct the CEGGPS patched module R_∞, M_∞, Π_∞ for GL_n beside PAPER-BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23's CEGGPS items, and the patched eigenvariety X_p(ρ̄) with its decomposition (5.8) into components of 𝔛_{ρ̄^p} × ∏_v X_tri(ρ̄_ṽ) × U^g. Carry the Taylor–Wiles hypotheses explicitly and separately — p > 2, F/F⁺ unramified with no non-trivial p-th root of 1 in F, G quasi-split at the finite places, U_v hyperspecial at the inert places, ρ̄ absolutely irreducible with adequate image — and note that the paper records these same hypotheses as having been **omitted** from its authors’ two earlier papers. Prove Lemmas 5.2.1–5.2.6 in the general form of p. 390 (any very strongly admissible Π^an), then prove classicality of generic crystalline strictly dominant points, the existence of all expected companion constituents by the descending induction on the patched eigenvariety, and Cohen–Macaulayness, flatness of the weight map and singularity at sufficiently critical points. Conjecture 5.1.1 and Conjecture 5.3.1 are conjectures and stay so; the crystalline hypothesis is expected to be removable but is not removed here.

routes.title: Locally analytic representations of p-adic reductive groups
routes.reason: PAPER-DING-25's new roadmap LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups owns the Orlik–Strauch functors with their irreducible constituents and Emerton's Jacquet functor with its adjunction (its brief (ii)–(iii)); this route joins it so that they have one owner (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/5, /8).
routes.brief: This route coalesces with LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, proposed by PAPER-DING-25 (route 1); keep its id, title, area and brief, whose parts (ii) and (iii) own the Orlik–Strauch functors F^G_{P^-}(M, π) with the theorem describing their irreducible constituents and Emerton's locally analytic Jacquet functor J_B with its adjunction. Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen add: very strongly admissible locally Q_p-analytic vectors of admissible unitary Banach representations; the Orlik–Strauch Jordan–Hölder theorem in the form used for the multiplicities m_{δ,Π} of their Conjecture 4.3.4 and Theorem 4.3.8 and for multiplicity one in Proposition 4.3.6; and, as a genuine obligation, the extension of the Orlik–Strauch and Emerton results from G(K) with G split reductive over K and L splitting K to products G_1(K_1) × G_2(K_2) with K_1 ≠ K_2 and L splitting both, which their Remark 5.1.2 asserts follows from an examination of the proofs. routes.reason: PG.7 is written for exactly the setting of §3.3: « the affinoid/relative Robba category of Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao », with the relative Herr and Iwasawa complexes, their finiteness and base change, and — as data/restructure/RS-26 records when it keeps that stage — triangulation and exceptional loci. The (φ,Γ_K)-modules over R_{A,K} and after inverting t, the characters with their weights and Lubin–Tate elements, and the cohomology with its comparison with Ext groups are therefore routed here rather than to the dagger-algebra stages: RD.0 owns the Robba ring as an analytic object and is cited alongside for the ring itself, but the (φ,Γ)-module theory and its cohomology belong to PG. routes.title: Representations of semisimple Lie algebras, highest weight theory, and the Weyl formulas, Part II: completed category O and analytic localization
routes.reason: LieHighestWeight plans PBW, Verma modules and L(λ) (Layer 3) and excludes category O; no stage plans category O, Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials or the Kazhdan–Lusztig theorem (RT-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/1). PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-25 route 3 opens the Part II that extends LieHighestWeight to category O, the extension in that roadmap's own direction (PROTOCOL.md section 15).
routes.brief: This route coalesces with LieHighestWeightPartIICompletedCategoryO, proposed by PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-25 (route 3); keep its id, title, parent, area and brief, which plans algebraic category O but no Kazhdan–Lusztig theory. Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen add, for a split reductive Lie algebra g ⊃ b ⊃ t over a field of characteristic 0: the block O(0) of the trivial infinitesimal character; the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials P_{x,y} of the Weyl group W, with P_{x,y} ≠ 0 if and only if x ≼ y and P_{x,x} = 1; and the Kazhdan–Lusztig multiplicity theorem [M(ww₀·0) : L(w′w₀·0)] = P_{w₀w,w₀w′}(1) (Beilinson–Bernstein 1981, Brylinski–Kashiwara 1981; Humphreys §8.4), as a stated input. Its proof by localisation needs D-modules on G/B and the Beilinson–Bernstein equivalence, which SpringerResolutionAndCharacteristicCycles builds; the design jobs must order those layers before the theorem, or keep it as a stated input. Consumers: SpringerResolutionAndCharacteristicCycles (Theorem 2.4.7(ii) and the cycle identities) and, through it, TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel.

prerequisites.citation: J.-M. Fontaine, Arithmétique des représentations galoisiennes p-adiques, in Cohomologies p-adiques et applications arithmétiques III, Astérisque 295 (2004), 1–115 [37]
prerequisites.why: The single most load-bearing input. §3.7 defines almost de Rham B_dR-representations; Th. 3.13 is the comparison isomorphism ρ_pdR; Th. 3.19 decomposes an almost de Rham representation into the B_dR[0;d]; Th. 4.1(2) characterises almost de Rham by dim_K D_pdR = dim W and Th. 4.1(3) identifies the jumps of the lattice filtration with the Sen weights; §4.3 constructs B⁺_pdR = B⁺_dR[log t] and the derivation ν; §2.7 and Th. 4.2 give B_pHT and the exactness of D_pHT. Everything in §§3.1–3.2 of this paper is a consumer of that theory.

prerequisites.citation: L. Berger, Construction de (φ,Γ)-modules: représentations p-adiques et B-paires, Algebra & Number Theory 2 (2008), 91–120 [9]
prerequisites.why: Th. 2.2.7, the equivalence between (φ,Γ_K)-modules over the Robba ring and B-pairs, and Prop. 2.2.6 with its parts (1) and (2), which give the functors W_e and W⁺_dR and their basic properties. Proposition 3.5.1 — the splitting of the deformation groupoid of D into a t-inverted part and a lattice part — is exactly an application of the B-pair formalism.

prerequisites.citation: K. Kedlaya, J. Pottharst and L. Xiao, Cohomology of arithmetic families of (φ,Γ)-modules, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 27 (2014), 1043–1115 [49]
prerequisites.why: Def. 6.2.1 and Cons. 6.2.4 for the Robba ring with coefficients and the rank-one modules R_{A,K}(δ); Not. 6.2.7 for the Lubin–Tate elements; Cor. 6.2.9 for the submodules of R_{L,K}(δ)[1/t]; Prop. 6.2.8 and Lem. 6.2.12 for the cohomology; and above all Th. 6.3.13 and Cor. 6.3.10, the existence of a triangulation with locally algebraic parameter and its globalisation after a proper birational modification, which is what makes Proposition 3.7.2 work.

prerequisites.citation: C. Breuil, E. Hellmann and B. Schraen, Une interprétation modulaire de la variété trianguline, Math. Ann. 367 (2017), 1587–1645 [19]
prerequisites.why: The construction of the trianguline variety X_tri(r̄) itself (§2.2), Th. 2.6 for its reducedness, equidimensionality and dimension and for the smoothness of the character map on U_tri(r̄), Prop. 2.9 identifying the weights of the parameter with the Sen weights, and §3.2 and §3.6 for the patched eigenvariety and its decomposition into components of 𝔛_{ρ̄^p} × ∏_v X_tri(ρ̄_ṽ) × U^g. The present paper assumes all of this. Note that its global results need the hypothesis ᵖ√1 ∉ F, which Remark 1.1 here records as having been omitted there.

prerequisites.citation: C. Breuil, E. Hellmann and B. Schraen, Smoothness and classicality on eigenvarieties, Invent. Math. 209 (2017), 197–274 [20]
prerequisites.why: Th. 3.9, the classicality criterion that Theorem 5.1.3 feeds with local irreducibility; Th. 1.3 and Conj. 2.8, the tangent-space bound that Proposition 4.1.5 recovers and Remark 4.1.6 sharpens; Lem. 2.1, Lem. 2.4, Lem. 2.7, §2.1 for strict dominance and refinements; Lem. 3.8 for the Cohen–Macaulay sheaf M_∞ on the patched eigenvariety; Th. 5.5 and Cor. 5.17–5.18 for the singularity argument. Two cautions recorded in this paper: the hypothesis ᵖ√1 ∉ F is missing from its Th. 1.1 and from §§3 and 5, and the proof of its Cor. 5.18 needs a Cohen–Macaulayness property that was overlooked there and is supplied by Proposition 5.4.1 here.

prerequisites.citation: R. Bezrukavnikov and S. Riche, Affine braid group actions on derived categories of Springer resolutions, Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. 45 (2012), 535–599 [12]
prerequisites.why: Th. 2.2.1, that the components of the Steinberg-type scheme are Cohen–Macaulay in characteristic greater than the Coxeter number, with Rem. 2.2.2(2) and Rem. 2.11.1 for the integral models used to descend to characteristic zero; and Prop. 2.14.2, identifying the cycle of the fibre X̄_w with the characteristic cycle of the Verma D-module. Proposition 2.3.3 and Proposition 2.4.6 of this paper are these results; the normality proved here (Theorem 2.3.6) is the new ingredient.

prerequisites.citation: J. E. Humphreys, Representations of semisimple Lie algebras in the BGG category O, Grad. Stud. Math. 94, AMS, 2008 [45]
prerequisites.why: §1.1–1.2 and §1.12 for category O, Verma modules and blocks; §8.4 for the Kazhdan–Lusztig multiplicity [M(ww₀·0) : L(w′w₀·0)] = P_{w₀w,w₀w′}(1); §0.3–0.4 for the length and Bruhat-order facts; §5.1–5.2 for strong linkage and the constituents of Verma modules; 8.3(a) for the vanishing used in the induction of §5.3. The whole cycle formalism of §2.4 and the multiplicity bookkeeping of §§4.3 and 5.3 run on these.

prerequisites.citation: R. Hotta, K. Takeuchi and T. Tanisaki, D-modules, perverse sheaves, and representation theory, Progr. Math. 236, Birkhäuser, 2008 [44]; with A. Beilinson and J. Bernstein, Localisation de g-modules, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 292 (1981), 15–18 [1]
prerequisites.why: (10.1.8) for t/W ≅ g/G, §6 and §11 for the Beilinson–Bernstein equivalence between category O and regular holonomic D-modules, Cor. 2.3.2 and Th. 2.2.3 for the dimension and additivity of characteristic cycles, and §10.3 for the identification of the cotangent bundle of G/B with the Springer resolution. This is the machine that turns Kazhdan–Lusztig multiplicities into cycles on the Steinberg variety.

prerequisites.citation: N. Chriss and V. Ginzburg, Representation theory and complex geometry, Birkhäuser, 1997 [27]; R. Steinberg, On the desingularization of the unipotent variety, Invent. Math. 36 (1976), 209–224 [62]
prerequisites.why: Prop. 3.3.4 and Cor. 3.3.5(ii) of Chriss–Ginzburg identify the Steinberg variety with the union of the conormal bundles of the diagonal G-orbits of G/B × G/B and its components with the closures of those conormal bundles; Steinberg is the origin of the variety itself.

prerequisites.citation: M. Kashiwara and Y. Saito, Geometric construction of crystal bases, Duke Math. J. 89 (1997), 9–36 [47]
prerequisites.why: The counterexample showing that the Kazhdan–Lusztig irreducibility conjecture on characteristic cycles fails for SL_n with n ≥ 8, recorded in Remark 2.4.5. A roadmap must not plan irreducibility of the cycles [𝔏(ww₀·0)].

prerequisites.citation: S. Orlik and M. Strauch, On Jordan–Hölder series of some locally analytic representations, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 28 (2015), 99–157 [58]
prerequisites.why: The functor F^G_{B̄} from category O and smooth representations to locally analytic representations, its finite length and the determination of its Jordan–Hölder constituents, plus Lem. 3.2 on integrating the b-action to a parabolic. The multiplicities m_{δ,Π} of the Breuil–Mézard statement and the companion constituents of §5.3 are defined through it. Remark 5.1.2 of this paper records that the results are stated in the literature for one split group over one field and extend, with the same proofs, to products over different fields — a gap a formalisation must close.

prerequisites.citation: C. Breuil, Vers le socle localement analytique pour GL_n I, Ann. Inst. Fourier 66 (2016), 633–685 [15]; and II, Math. Ann. 361 (2015), 741–785 [16]
prerequisites.why: [15, §2] and [15, Cor. 2.7] for the Orlik–Strauch formalism and multiplicity one, [15, §6] for the companion constituents; [16, Th. 4.3] for the reformulation of membership in the eigenvariety, [16, Prop. 4.2] for the adjunction of Lemma 5.2.1, and above all [16, Conj. 6.1], [16, Conj. 6.2] and [16, Conj. 6.6] — the socle and companion-point conjectures of which Theorem 4.2.3 is the local analogue and Theorem 5.3.3 a case.

prerequisites.citation: A. Caraiani, M. Emerton, T. Gee, D. Geraghty, V. Paškūnas and S.-W. Shin, Patching and the p-adic local Langlands correspondence, Camb. J. Math. 4 (2016), 197–287 [23]
